FunctionBodyPart@kerml.decision: Any number of body elements or return features, then an optional result expression. The result expression comes last and at most once, which is what makes the final expression in a body its value.

FunctionOperationExpression.decision: '->' then the invoked function, then exactly one of three argument forms: a body, a function reference, or an ordinary argument list. None of the three is optional, so an operation always takes one. The member after '->' is InstantiatedTypeMember; the clause's own InvocationTypeMember is defined nowhere and is a specification defect the editor has acknowledged. See the deviation InvocationTypeMember-misnomer.

FunctionReference.decision: `ownedRelationship += ReferenceTyping`. A function is named by typing a reference, the same mechanism TypeReference uses.

FunctionReferenceExpression.decision: `ownedRelationship += FunctionReferenceMember`. Unlike FeatureReferenceExpression in the sibling clause, this one carries no EmptyResultMember.

GeneralType@kerml.decision: As KerML 8.2.4.1.2 states it: `general = [QualifiedName]`, or `general += OwnedFeatureChain` with the chain owned by the relationship. The cross-reference parses a QualifiedName, and the `{ ownedRelatedElement += general }` action consumes no tokens. The pilot Xtext has no rule of this name, so there is no second opinion. It inlines this body into each rule that uses it.

GuardExpressionMember@sysml.decision: SysML 8.2.2.18.3 states `'if' { kind = 'guard' } ownedRelatedElement += OwnedExpression`. The braced part assigns into the abstract syntax and contributes no token, so the rule is the keyword followed by the expression. The Xtext writes `kind = GuardFeatureKind ownedRelatedElement += OwnedExpression`, and GuardFeatureKind (SysML.xtext:1905) is an enum whose only literal is `guard = 'if'`, so the two accept the same keyword. The guard is a full OwnedExpression rather than anything narrower, which is what admits the conjunction on SimpleVehicleModel line 59; narrowing it to a simpler expression form would be the kind of range narrowing a parser generator wants and the language does not state.

GuardedSuccession@sysml.decision: A transcription of SysML 8.2.2.17.8. The Xtext agrees on every token and differs only in two names and one abstract-syntax member, none of which changes the language. SuccessionKeyword is an alias for the single literal 'succession' (SysML.xtext:1027). TransitionSourceMember is the Xtext's local name for the clause's FeatureChainMember: SysML.xtext:1884 gives it `memberElement = [Feature|QualifiedName] | ownedRelatedElement += OwnedFeatureChain`, which is FeatureChainMember's own text in 8.2.2.17.5, and only FeatureChainMember has a unit. The Xtext also inserts `ownedRelationship += EmptyParameterMember` between the source and the guard, which the clause omits; it contributes no tokens, so it is a difference in the abstract syntax the pilot builds rather than in the syntax it accepts, and the clause is followed. The guard is not optional here — that is what separates a guarded succession from a plain one, whose declaration carries no 'if'.

GuardedSuccessionMember@sysml.decision: SysML 8.2.2.17.1 states GuardedSuccessionMember : FeatureMembership = MemberPrefix ownedRelatedElement += GuardedSuccession. The SysML Xtext is identical. The rule is the clause as written.

GuardedTargetSuccession@sysml.decision: A transcription of SysML 8.2.2.17.8. The Xtext accepts the same tokens in the same order and differs only by a leading `ownedRelationship += EmptyParameterMember`, which contributes no tokens: a difference in the abstract syntax the pilot builds, not in the syntax it accepts, so the clause is followed. Unlike GuardedSuccession this production has no 'first' source and no declaration — its source is the body item that precedes it — which is what makes it the target form. The guard is mandatory, and it is the only thing separating it from the plain TargetSuccession stated two lines above it in the same clause.

Identification.decision: As KerML 8.2.3.1 and SysML 8.2.2.2 both state it, in the same words, so one shared unit: an optional short name in angle brackets, then an optional name. Both parts are optional, so Identification derives the empty string, and every production that uses it admits an anonymous element. The Xtext fragment is not nullable: `'<' Name '>' Name? | Name` requires at least one name. That is a real difference in this production, but not necessarily in the language, because a caller can restore the empty case by writing `Identification?`. Whether every Xtext caller does so is not visible from this pack, and phase 5's oracle is where a gap would show. The clause is the source and is followed. A recursive-descent implementation must treat Identification as possibly empty.

IfNode@sysml.decision: A transcription of SysML 8.2.2.17.7. The clause and the Xtext state this production identically, token for token (SysML.xtext:1596), so there is nothing to weigh. The else branch's choice between an ActionBodyParameterMember and an IfNodeParameterMember is what makes `else if` a chain rather than a special form: the second alternative nests another IfNode in the else position, and the clause's own recursion through IfNodeParameterMember is what terminates it.

IfNodeParameterMember@sysml.decision: A transcription of SysML 8.2.2.17.7. The clause and the Xtext state this production identically — `ownedRelatedElement += IfNode` in both — so there is nothing to weigh. It contributes no tokens, and its only purpose is to sit in IfNode's else position so that an else branch may be another if. That is what makes `else if` a nesting of this production rather than a separate keyword pair, and it is the source of the rule's recursion.

Import.decision: A visibility indicator, `import`, an optional `all`, the declaration, and a relationship body, as KerML 8.2.3.4.2 states it. THE VISIBILITY IS MANDATORY HERE, and that is the one thing about this production most likely to be got wrong: everywhere else in the language visibility arrives through the nullable MemberPrefix, but Import states `visibility = VisibilityIndicator` with no `?`. An import must say whether it is public, private or protected.

ImportDeclaration.decision: A membership import or a namespace import, as KerML 8.2.3.4.2 and SysML 8.2.2.5.1 both state it.

IncludeUseCaseUsage@sysml.decision: SysML 8.2.2.25 states IncludeUseCaseUsage : OccurrenceUsagePrefix 'include' ( ownedRelationship += OwnedReferenceSubsetting FeatureSpecializationPart? | 'use' 'case' UsageDeclaration ) ValuePart? CaseBody. The SysML Xtext writes UsageDeclaration? and factors 'use' 'case' into a keyword rule; UsageDeclaration is already nullable, so neither changes the language. The clause's header is `IncludeUseCaseUsage :` with no '=' and no result type; the body is unambiguous and is taken as written. The rule is the clause as written.

IndexExpression.decision: `#` then a parenthesised sequence. Distinct from BracketExpression, which uses square brackets and no `#`.

IndividualDefinition@sysml.decision: SysML 8.2.2.9.1 states IndividualDefinition : OccurrenceDefinition = BasicDefinitionPrefix? isIndividual ?= 'individual' DefinitionExtensionKeyword* 'def' Definition ownedRelationship += EmptyMultiplicityMember, and the SysML Xtext agrees (the same elements, with EmptyMultiplicityMember placed after 'individual' instead of after Definition). The rule is the clause as written. The Xtext's position for EmptyMultiplicityMember differs; the same clause defines EmptyMultiplicity as `{ }`, which consumes no tokens, so its position does not change what is accepted and the clause's order is kept.

IndividualUsage@sysml.decision: SysML 8.2.2.9.2 states IndividualUsage : OccurrenceUsage = BasicUsagePrefix isIndividual ?= 'individual' UsageExtensionKeyword* Usage. The SysML Xtext is identical. The rule is the clause as written.

InitialNodeMember@sysml.decision: SysML 8.2.2.17.1 states InitialNodeMember : FeatureMembership = MemberPrefix 'first' memberFeature = [QualifiedName] RelationshipBody. The SysML Xtext returns SysML::Membership and assigns memberElement, the same syntax. The rule is the clause as written.

InstantiatedTypeMember.decision: A named type, or an owned feature chain. The second alternative is why `x->a.b.select {...}` can name the operation by a chain rather than a single name.

InstantiatedTypeReference.decision: `[QualifiedName]`, typed as a Type rather than a Feature. Same text as FeatureReference and InstantiatedTypeReference differs only in what it builds.

Interaction@kerml.decision: KerML 8.2.5.9.1 states Interaction = TypePrefix 'interaction' ClassifierDeclaration TypeBody. The KerML Xtext is identical. The rule is the clause as written.

InterfaceBody@sysml.decision: SysML 8.2.2.14.1 states InterfaceBody : Type = ';' | '{' InterfaceBodyItem* '}'. The SysML Xtext is identical. The rule is the clause as written.

InterfaceBodyItem@sysml.decision: SysML 8.2.2.14.1 states InterfaceBodyItem : Type = ownedRelationship += DefinitionMember | ownedRelationship += VariantUsageMember | ownedRelationship += InterfaceNonOccurrenceUsageMember | ( ownedRelationship += SourceSuccessionMember )? ownedRelationship += InterfaceOccurrenceUsageMember | ownedRelationship += AliasMember | ownedRelationship += Import. The SysML Xtext writes the same alternatives, naming the optional leading member EmptySuccessionMember and putting a `=>` predicate on Import; the renaming and the predicate are not ported. The rule is the clause as written.

InterfaceDefinition@sysml.decision: SysML 8.2.2.14.1 states OccurrenceDefinitionPrefix 'interface' 'def' DefinitionDeclaration InterfaceBody, and the SysML Xtext agrees (the same structure; the keyword pair is factored into a keyword rule, a renaming). The rule is the clause as written.

InterfaceEnd@sysml.decision: A transcription of SysML 8.2.2.14.2. REFERENCES is one of the special lexical terminals of 8.2.2.1.2 and is written out as its keyword alternatives, `'::>' | 'references'`, following the convention used for TYPED_BY and the rest; the Xtext's ReferencesKeyword (SysML.xtext:415) spells the same two literals. The Xtext's `declaredName = Name` against the clause's `declaredName = NAME` is the same position, and NAME is the terminal the specification names, so the token is written as NAME. Nothing else differs. The named-end form is what makes `mqget ::> ...` legal inside an n-ary interface part, where an end needs a name to be referred to later; the binary form usually omits it.

InterfaceEndMember@sysml.decision: A transcription of SysML 8.2.2.14.2. The clause and the Xtext state this production identically — `ownedRelatedElement += InterfaceEnd` in both — so there is nothing to weigh. It contributes no tokens of its own; the text of an end is entirely in InterfaceEnd, and the 'to' of the binary form and the brackets and commas of the n-ary form belong to BinaryInterfacePart and NaryInterfacePart respectively. That is what lets one member production serve both.

InterfaceNonOccurrenceUsageElement@sysml.decision: SysML 8.2.2.14.1 states InterfaceNonOccurrenceUsageElement : Usage = ReferenceUsage | AttributeUsage | EnumerationUsage | BindingConnectorAsUsage | SuccessionAsUsage. The SysML Xtext is identical. The rule is the clause as written.

InterfaceNonOccurrenceUsageMember@sysml.decision: SysML 8.2.2.14.1 states InterfaceNonOccurrenceUsageMember : FeatureMembership = MemberPrefix ownedRelatedElement += InterfaceNonOccurrenceUsageElement. The SysML Xtext is identical. The rule is the clause as written.

InterfaceOccurrenceUsageElement@sysml.decision: SysML 8.2.2.14.1 states InterfaceOccurrenceUsageElement : Usage = DefaultInterfaceEnd | StructureUsageElement | BehaviorUsageElement. The SysML Xtext is identical. The rule is the clause as written.

InterfaceOccurrenceUsageMember@sysml.decision: SysML 8.2.2.14.1 states InterfaceOccurrenceUsageMember : FeatureMembership = MemberPrefix ownedRelatedElement += InterfaceOccurrenceUsageElement. The SysML Xtext is identical. The rule is the clause as written.

InterfacePart@sysml.decision: SysML 8.2.2.14.2 states InterfacePart : InterfaceUsage = BinaryInterfacePart | NaryInterfacePart. The SysML Xtext is the same syntax, returning SysML::ConnectionUsage. The rule is the clause as written.

InterfaceUsage@sysml.decision: SysML 8.2.2.14.2 states InterfaceUsage = OccurrenceUsagePrefix 'interface' InterfaceUsageDeclaration InterfaceBody. The SysML Xtext factors the keyword into a keyword rule, a renaming. The rule is the clause as written.

InterfaceUsageDeclaration@sysml.decision: SysML 8.2.2.14.2 states InterfaceUsageDeclaration : InterfaceUsage = UsageDeclaration ValuePart? ( 'connect' InterfacePart )? | InterfacePart. The SysML Xtext writes UsageDeclaration? and factors 'connect' into a keyword rule; UsageDeclaration is already nullable, so neither changes the language. The rule is the clause as written.

Intersecting@kerml.decision: As KerML 8.2.4.1.5 states it: the intersecting type, as a cross-reference `[QualifiedName]` or as an owned OwnedFeatureChain. The Xtext rule is identical.

IntersectingPart@kerml.decision: As KerML 8.2.4.1.1 states it: 'intersects', then one or more Intersecting separated by commas. The Xtext fragment is identical. The leading keyword is unique among TypeRelationshipPart's four alternatives in the same clause (`disjoint from`, `unions`, `intersects`, `differences`), so the alternatives do not overlap. TypeDeclaration, in the same clause, repeats relationship parts with `TypeRelationshipPart*`, so the same part may occur more than once. Repeating the keyword and continuing the comma list both accept a further target.

Invariant@kerml.decision: A feature prefix, `inv`, an optional `true`/`false`, an optional declaration, an optional value and a function body. The declaration is OPTIONAL, which is now corroborated three ways: KERML11-181 names this clause, the Xtext already accepts it, and the corpus contains `inv { age >= 35 }` which the clause as printed rejects. `isNegated ?=` is an abstract-syntax assignment, not concrete syntax, so the rule carries the keywords and not the assignment.

InvertingPart@kerml.decision: As KerML 8.2.4.3.1 states it: the two keywords `inverse of`, then exactly one OwnedFeatureInverting, with no comma-separated repetition. The Xtext fragment is identical. The pack's corpus instances were matched on the word `of` alone, and most of them are prose or flow declarations, not instances of this rule. The corpus evidence below was found separately by searching for `inverse of`.

InvocationExpression.decision: The type being invoked, its arguments, and the empty result. The member is InstantiatedTypeMember; the clause writes InstatiatedTypeMember, missing an 'n', which is recorded as the deviation InstatiatedTypeMember-misspelling.

ItemDefinition@sysml.decision: SysML 8.2.2.10 states OccurrenceDefinitionPrefix 'item' 'def' Definition, and the SysML Xtext agrees (the same structure; the keyword pair is factored into a keyword rule, a renaming). The rule is the clause as written.

ItemUsage@sysml.decision: SysML 8.2.2.10 states ItemUsage = OccurrenceUsagePrefix 'item' Usage. The SysML Xtext factors the keyword into a keyword rule, a renaming. The rule is the clause as written.

JoinNode@sysml.decision: A transcription of SysML 8.2.2.17.3: `ControlNodePrefix isComposite ?= 'join' UsageDeclaration ActionBody`. The `isComposite ?=` assigns into the abstract syntax and contributes no token. The Xtext's `UsageDeclaration?` is redundant against the clause's `UsageDeclaration`, since UsageDeclaration is nullable through Identification. The four control nodes are identical below their keyword, which is why they are told apart on one token.

LibraryPackage.decision: KerML 8.2.5.13 and SysML 8.2.2.5.1 print `( isStandard ?= 'standard' ) 'library'` with no '?' on the group; the KerML Xtext makes the group optional. That disagreement is adjudicated and recorded as deviation LibraryPackage (follow_xtext): the missing '?' is a defect printed in both documents, contradicted by KerML's own example and the isStandard attribute, and the corpus writes `library package` without 'standard'. The rest of the rule is the clauses as written, which agree with the Xtext.

LiteralExpression.decision: Five alternatives, in the clause's order.

LiteralInteger.decision: `value = DECIMAL_VALUE`, the lexical terminal from KerML 8.2.2.4.

LiteralString.decision: `value = STRING_VALUE`, the lexical terminal from KerML 8.2.2.5.

MemberElement@kerml.decision: Two alternatives, as KerML 8.2.3.4.3 states them: an annotating element, or a non-feature element. Together with FeatureElement in the same clause, this is what partitions everything that can be a member of a namespace — the clause states all three productions side by side and MemberElement is the half that is not a feature.

MemberPrefix.decision: An optional visibility indicator, and nothing else, exactly as KerML 8.2.3.4.1 states it. Every membership production in the language opens with this, which is why it is a production of its own rather than an option repeated at each site.

MembershipExpose@sysml.decision: SysML 8.2.2.26.2 states this production in one line: `MembershipExpose = MembershipImport`. An expose of a single membership is written exactly as an import of it, and the difference lives entirely in the enclosing Expose. The Xtext writes `ExposePrefix ImportedMembership`, which differs in two ways that cancel: ExposePrefix (SysML.xtext:2366) is the 'expose' keyword encoded as a visibility assignment, and this derivation puts that keyword in Expose where the clause puts it, so it must not appear again here; and ImportedMembership is the Xtext's name for the body of the clause's MembershipImport. The clause's form is taken, and the keyword is stated once.

MembershipImport.decision: A qualified name, optionally followed by `::**` to import recursively, as KerML 8.2.3.4.2 states it and SysML repeats.

MergeNode@sysml.decision: A transcription of SysML 8.2.2.17.3: `ControlNodePrefix isComposite ?= 'merge' UsageDeclaration ActionBody`. The `isComposite ?=` is an assignment into the abstract syntax attached to the keyword, not a token, so the concrete rule is the keyword itself. The Xtext writes `UsageDeclaration?` where the clause writes `UsageDeclaration`; that is redundant rather than wider, because UsageDeclaration is `Identification FeatureSpecializationPart?` (8.2.2.6.2) and Identification is `( '<' NAME '>' )? ( declaredName = NAME )?` (8.2.2.2), so it already derives empty. The two accept the same language — the MultiplicityRange@kerml case again — and the clause's form is kept, so no deviation is recorded.

Message@sysml.decision: SysML 8.2.2.16 states Message : FlowUsage = OccurrenceUsagePrefix 'message' MessageDeclaration DefinitionBody { isAbstract = true }. The SysML Xtext factors the keyword into a keyword rule, a renaming. The `{ isAbstract = true }` action is abstract syntax. The rule is the clause as written.

MessageDeclaration@sysml.decision: SysML 8.2.2.16 states MessageDeclaration : FlowUsage = UsageDeclaration ValuePart? ( 'of' ownedRelationship += FlowPayloadFeatureMember )? ( 'from' ownedRelationship += MessageEventMember 'to' ownedRelationship += MessageEventMember )? | ownedRelationship += MessageEventMember 'to' ownedRelationship += MessageEventMember. The SysML Xtext writes UsageDeclaration? and PayloadFeatureMember where the clause writes FlowPayloadFeatureMember; UsageDeclaration is already nullable, and the payload member is not ported, since the clause names its own production. The rule is the clause as written.

MessageEvent@sysml.decision: A transcription of SysML 8.2.2.16. The clause and the Xtext state this production identically — `ownedRelationship += OwnedReferenceSubsetting` in both — so there is nothing to weigh. A message event is nothing but a reference to the occurrence it names: it carries no keyword, no declaration and no body of its own, and everything that makes it an end of a message ('from', 'to', and the MessageEventMember wrapper) belongs to the productions around it. That is what lets the same subsetting reference serve as either end.

MessageEventMember@sysml.decision: SysML 8.2.2.16 states MessageEventMember : ParameterMembership = ownedRelatedElement += MessageEvent. The SysML Xtext is identical. The rule is the clause as written.

Metaclass@kerml.decision: KerML 8.2.5.12 states Metaclass = TypePrefix 'metaclass' ClassifierDeclaration TypeBody. The KerML Xtext is identical. The rule is the clause as written.

MetaclassificationExpression.decision: A metadata argument, then a metaclass test or a metacast, then the empty result. Structurally the same shape as ClassificationExpression, with two differences the clause makes deliberately: the operand is a MetadataArgumentMember rather than an ArgumentMember, because a metaclassification tests an element reference and not a value, and the operand is NOT optional here where ClassificationExpression's is. The operator is spelled MetaclassificationTestOperator, lowercase c, which the clause defines; the clause's own reference to a capital-C spelling resolves to nothing and is recorded as the deviation MetaClassificationTestOperator-casing.

MetaclassificationTestOperator.decision: One literal. The metaclass counterpart of ClassificationTestOperator's `@`.

MetadataAccessExpression.decision: An element reference followed by `.metadata`. Both the dot and the keyword are literal and neither is optional.

MetadataBody@kerml.decision: KerML 8.2.5.12 states MetadataBody : Feature = ';' | '{' ( ownedRelationship += MetadataBodyElement )* '}'. The KerML Xtext expands MetadataBodyElement into NonFeatureMember | MetadataBodyFeatureMember | AliasMember | Import. The expansion is not ported; the rule is the clause as written.

MetadataBody@sysml.decision: SysML 8.2.2.27 states MetadataBody : Type = ';' | '{' ( ownedRelationship += DefinitionMember | ownedRelationship += MetadataBodyUsageMember | ownedRelationship += AliasMember | ownedRelationship += Import )* '}'. The SysML Xtext is the same syntax, returning SysML::Usage. The rule is the clause as written.

MetadataBodyElement@kerml.decision: KerML 8.2.5.12 states MetadataBodyElement : Membership = NonFeatureMember | MetadataBodyFeatureMember | AliasMember | Import. The pilot Xtext has no such rule; KerML.xtext's MetadataBody inlines the same four alternatives. The rule is the clause as written.

MetadataBodyFeature@kerml.decision: KerML 8.2.5.12 states MetadataBodyFeature : Feature = 'feature'? ( ':>>' | 'redefines' )? ownedRelationship += OwnedRedefinition FeatureSpecializationPart? ValuePart? MetadataBody. The clause writes the redefinition keyword pair out literally rather than as REDEFINES. The KerML Xtext is identical. The rule is the clause as written.

MetadataBodyFeatureMember@kerml.decision: KerML 8.2.5.12 states MetadataBodyFeatureMember : FeatureMembership = ownedMemberFeature = MetadataBodyFeature. The KerML Xtext assigns it to ownedRelatedElement instead, the same syntax. The rule is the clause as written.

MetadataBodyUsage@sysml.decision: SysML 8.2.2.27 states MetadataBodyUsage : ReferenceUsage : 'ref'? ( ':>>' | 'redefines' )? ownedRelationship += OwnedRedefinition FeatureSpecializationPart? ValuePart? MetadataBody. The SysML Xtext is identical. The header ends in ':' where '=' belongs; the body is unambiguous and is taken as written. The rule is the clause as written.

MetadataBodyUsageMember@sysml.decision: SysML 8.2.2.27 states MetadataBodyUsageMember : FeatureMembership = ownedMemberFeature = MetadataBodyUsage. The SysML Xtext assigns to ownedRelatedElement, the same syntax. The rule is the clause as written.

MetadataDefinition@sysml.decision: SysML 8.2.2.27 states MetadataDefinition = ( isAbstract ?= 'abstract' )? DefinitionExtensionKeyWord* 'metadata' 'def' Definition. DefinitionExtensionKeyWord, with a capital W, is defined nowhere; the production is DefinitionExtensionKeyword, and the same clause's ExtendedDefinition spells it so. Recorded as deviation DefinitionExtensionKeyWord-casing (follow_spec, the defined spelling). The SysML Xtext agrees with the repaired rule. Otherwise the rule is the clause as written.

MetadataFeature@kerml.decision: KerML 8.2.5.12 states MetadataFeature = ( ownedRelationship += PrefixMetadataMember )* ( '@' | 'metadata' ) MetadataFeatureDeclaration ( 'about' ownedRelationship += Annotation ( ',' ownedRelationship += Annotation )* )? MetadataBody. The KerML Xtext is identical. The rule is the clause as written.

MetadataFeatureDeclaration@kerml.decision: KerML 8.2.5.12 states MetadataFeatureDeclaration : MetadataFeature = ( Identification ( ':' | 'typed' 'by' ) )? ownedRelationship += OwnedFeatureTyping. The KerML Xtext writes Identification? where the clause writes Identification; the specification's Identification (KerML 8.2.3.1) is ( '<' NAME '>' )? NAME? and can already be empty, so the '?' adds nothing, and types the feature by MetadataTyping where the clause writes OwnedFeatureTyping. That narrowing is the one adjudicated as deviation PrefixMetadataTyping-chain (follow_spec), which covers all four metadata typings in KerML 8.2.5.12, so the clause's OwnedFeatureTyping is kept. The rule is the clause as written.

MetadataReference.decision: `ownedRelationship += ElementReferenceMember`, typed as a MetadataAccessExpression. The operand of a metaclassification is a reference to an element, not an expression over values, which is what makes `@@` a test on the metaclass rather than on the value.

MetadataUsage@sysml.decision: SysML 8.2.2.27 states MetadataUsage = UsageExtensionKeyword* ( '@' | 'metadata' ) MetadataUsageDeclaration ( 'about' ownedRelationship += Annotation ( ',' ownedRelationship += Annotation )* )? MetadataBody. The SysML Xtext writes the same, with the keyword pair factored into MetadataUsageKeyword, a renaming. The rule is the clause as written.

MetadataUsageDeclaration@sysml.decision: SysML 8.2.2.27 states MetadataUsageDeclaration : MetadataUsage = ( Identification ( ':' | 'typed' 'by' ) )? ownedRelationship += OwnedFeatureTyping. Deviation MetadataUsageDeclaration (follow_xtext) reads the keyword pair as SysML's DEFINED_BY, ':' | 'defined' 'by'. The typing stays OwnedFeatureTyping as the clause prints it, not the Xtext's MetadataTyping, per deviation PrefixMetadataTyping-chain.

Multiplicity@kerml.decision: KerML 8.2.5.11 states Multiplicity = MultiplicitySubset | MultiplicityRange. The KerML Xtext is identical. The rule is the clause as written.

MultiplicityBounds@kerml.decision: As KerML 8.2.5.11 states it: `[`, an optional lower bound followed by `..`, the upper bound, and `]`. So a single member is the upper bound. The Xtext groups it the other way, as `'[' member ( '..' member )? ']'`, which accepts the same token sequences. It differs only in whether a lone member is the first or the second member, and that is a matter for the abstract syntax, where the clause governs. The Xtext also carries a TODO to allow general expressions for the bounds, which 'causes LL parsing issues'. The clause does not allow them either: MultiplicityExpressionMember is limited to a LiteralExpression or a FeatureReferenceExpression. So nothing is narrowed relative to the specification, and nothing is ported.

MultiplicityExpressionMember.decision: As KerML 8.2.5.11 and SysML 8.2.2.6.6 both state it, so one shared unit: a bound is a LiteralExpression or a FeatureReferenceExpression, never a general expression. The limit is the specification's own, not an Xtext workaround. The Xtext rule is identical, and its TODO about general expressions is an aspiration of the pilot, not a statement of the language.

MultiplicityPart.decision: As KerML 8.2.4.3.1 and SysML 8.2.2.6.6 both state it, so one shared unit. Either a multiplicity alone, or an optional multiplicity followed by `ordered` and `nonunique` in either order, each at most once. The `{ isUnique = false }` actions set properties and consume no tokens. The Xtext writes `isUnique = Nonunique`, calling a one-keyword rule where the clause writes the literal 'nonunique'. The token sequence is identical, and the rule follows the clause's literal. The two outer alternatives do not overlap: the second always ends in `ordered` or `nonunique`, and the first never contains either.

MultiplicityRange@kerml.decision: As KerML 8.2.5.11 states it: `multiplicity`, an Identification, MultiplicityBounds and a TypeBody. This is the KerML variant (ADR-0014); in SysML, MultiplicityRange is the bracketed form alone. The Xtext writes `Identification?` where the clause writes `Identification`. The two accept the same language. The specification's Identification (KerML 8.2.3.1) is `( '<' NAME '>' )? ( NAME )?` and can derive the empty string, so an anonymous `multiplicity [0..1];` already parses by the clause. The pilot's Identification fragment requires at least one name, so its `?` here restores what the specification allows. The rule follows the clause and needs no deviation.

MultiplicityRange@sysml.decision: As SysML 8.2.2.6.6 states it: `[`, an optional lower bound followed by `..`, the upper bound, and `]`. This is the SysML variant (ADR-0014): in SysML, MultiplicityRange is the bracketed form itself. The Xtext groups it as `'[' member ( '..' member )? ']'`, which accepts the same token sequences. It carries a TODO that general expressions for bounds cause LL parsing issues, but the clause's MultiplicityExpressionMember is already limited to a LiteralExpression or a FeatureReferenceExpression. So nothing is narrowed relative to the specification.

MultiplicitySubset@kerml.decision: KerML 8.2.5.11 states MultiplicitySubset : Multiplicity = 'multiplicity' Identification Subsets TypeBody. The KerML Xtext writes Identification? where the clause writes Identification; the specification's Identification (KerML 8.2.3.1) is ( '<' NAME '>' )? NAME? and can already be empty, so the '?' adds nothing. The rule is the clause as written.

NamedArgument.decision: The parameter being named, then `=`, then the value. The left side is a redefinition rather than a plain name, which is what ties a named argument to the parameter it supplies.

NamedArgumentList.decision: One or more NamedArgumentMembers, comma separated.

Namespace@kerml.decision: KerML 8.2.3.4.1 states Namespace = ( ownedRelationship += PrefixMetadataMember )* NamespaceDeclaration NamespaceBody. The KerML Xtext is identical. The rule is the clause as written.

NamespaceBody@kerml.decision: KerML 8.2.3.4.1 states NamespaceBody : Namespace = ';' | '{' NamespaceBodyElement* '}'. The KerML Xtext expands NamespaceBodyElement into NamespaceMember | AliasMember | Import, and its own comment says this is 'to avoid infinite loops in the incremental parser' — an LL workaround, not ported. The rule is the clause as written.

NamespaceBodyElement@kerml.decision: Three alternatives, as KerML 8.2.3.4.1 states them: a namespace member, an alias member, or an import. This is what a KerML root namespace, and a KerML namespace body, is a sequence of.

NamespaceDeclaration@kerml.decision: KerML 8.2.3.4.1 states NamespaceDeclaration : Namespace = 'namespace' Identification. The KerML Xtext writes Identification? where the clause writes Identification; the specification's Identification (KerML 8.2.3.1) is ( '<' NAME '>' )? NAME? and can already be empty, so the '?' adds nothing. The rule is the clause as written.

NamespaceExpose@sysml.decision: SysML 8.2.2.26.2 states this production in one line: `NamespaceExpose = NamespaceImport`. The Xtext writes `ExposePrefix ( ImportedNamespace | ownedRelatedElement += FilterPackage )`, which looks wider and is not. The clause's NamespaceImport (8.2.2.5.1) already has exactly those two alternatives: `importedNamespace = [QualifiedName] '::' '*' ( '::' isRecursive ?= '**' )?` and `importedNamspace = FilterPackage`. ImportedNamespace is simply the Xtext's name for the first. ExposePrefix (SysML.xtext:2366) is the 'expose' keyword, which this derivation states once in Expose, as the clause does, so it does not reappear here. Both readings therefore accept the same text and the clause's form is taken.

NamespaceFeatureMember@kerml.decision: A member prefix and a feature element, as KerML 8.2.3.4.1 states it.

NamespaceImport.decision: Either a qualified name followed by `::*`, optionally `::**` to recurse, or a filter package — as KerML 8.2.3.4.2 states it and SysML repeats.

NamespaceMember@kerml.decision: A non-feature member or a namespace feature member, as KerML 8.2.3.4.1 states it.

NaryConnectorDeclaration@kerml.decision: KerML 8.2.5.5.1 states NaryConnectorDeclaration : Connector = FeatureDeclaration? '(' ownedRelationship += ConnectorEndMember ',' ownedRelationship += ConnectorEndMember ( ',' ownedRelationship += ConnectorEndMember )* ')'. The KerML Xtext is identical. The rule is the clause as written.

NaryConnectorPart@sysml.decision: SysML 8.2.2.13.1 states NaryConnectorPart : ConnectionUsage = '(' ownedRelationship += ConnectorEndMember ',' ownedRelationship += ConnectorEndMember ( ',' ownedRelationship += ConnectorEndMember )* ')'. The SysML Xtext is the same syntax, returning SysML::Connector. The rule is the clause as written.

NaryInterfacePart@sysml.decision: A transcription of SysML 8.2.2.14.2. The clause and the Xtext state this production identically; the Xtext writes it as a `fragment`, an inlining mechanism of that parser generator rather than a claim about the language, and the specification names it as a production that InterfacePart selects. The two mandatory ends before the repetition are the clause's own shape and are kept: they make two the minimum, so `( a )` is not an n-ary interface part, and the binary form without brackets remains the only way to write exactly two. The repetition is a star rather than a separator list because the clause spells it that way, and writing it out keeps the minimum of two visible in the rule itself.

NodeParameter@sysml.decision: A transcription of SysML 8.2.2.17.4. The clause and the Xtext state this production identically — `ownedRelationship += FeatureBinding` in both — so there is nothing to weigh. It contributes no tokens; the expression it stands for is reached through FeatureBinding, which is a FeatureValue over an OwnedExpression. Being an expression rather than a name is what lets a send payload be `new S()` or a for-loop sequence be `(1, 2, 3)`.

NodeParameterMember@sysml.decision: A transcription of SysML 8.2.2.17.4. The clause and the Xtext state this production identically — `ownedRelatedElement += NodeParameter` in both — so there is nothing to weigh. It contributes no tokens of its own; everything visible is the expression below it, reached through NodeParameter and its FeatureBinding. It is the parameter position that the send, terminate and for-loop nodes all use, which is why one member serves a payload, a terminated occurrence and an iterated sequence alike.

NonBehaviorBodyItem@sysml.decision: SysML 8.2.2.17.1 states NonBehaviorBodyItem = ownedRelationship += Import | ownedRelationship += AliasMember | ownedRelationship += DefinitionMember | ownedRelationship += VariantUsageMember | ownedRelationship += NonOccurrenceUsageMember | ( ownedRelationship += SourceSuccessionMember )? ownedRelationship += StructureUsageMember. The SysML Xtext has no NonBehaviorBodyItem rule; it inlines these alternatives into ActionBodyItem and StateBodyItem. The rule is the clause as written.

NonFeatureChainPrimaryArgumentMember.decision: `ownedMemberParameter = PrimaryArgument`, as both sources state it, and NOT NonFeatureChainPrimaryArgument despite this production's name. Derived as written for two reasons. The clause and Tier B' agree. And the reading is defensible on its own terms: FeatureChainExpression is the only production that uses this member, and allowing its left operand to be a chain is what makes `a.b.c` group as `(a.b).c`. The Pilot builds exactly that association, with `{FeatureChainExpression.operand += current}` inside a repetition (KerMLExpressions.xtext:301, :319), which is the Xtext idiom for a left-associative fold. A restriction to non-chain operands would forbid it.

NonFeatureChainPrimaryExpression.decision: Seven alternatives, in the clause's order. Everything primary that is not a feature chain.

NonFeatureElement@kerml.decision: Twenty-six alternatives, as KerML 8.2.3.4.3 states them, in the clause's order. The Xtext lists the same twenty-six in a different order. Order in an alternation does not change the language the grammar describes, and the rule follows the clause's order. The alternatives are the non-feature declarations: namespaces, packages, types and their kinds, and the standalone relationship declarations. None is defined in this pack, so their overlap is for their own units.

NonFeatureMember@kerml.decision: A member prefix and a member element, exactly as KerML 8.2.3.4.1 states it. No keyword of its own: this is the plain, unannounced way a non-feature element becomes a member of a namespace, and it is the case that carries most of what a file contains.

NonOccurrenceUsageElement@sysml.decision: SysML 8.2.2.6.4 states NonOccurrenceUsageElement : Usage = DefaultReferenceUsage | ReferenceUsage | AttributeUsage | EnumerationUsage | BindingConnectorAsUsage | SuccessionAsUsage | ExtendedUsage, and the SysML Xtext agrees (identical). The rule is the clause as written.

NonOccurrenceUsageMember@sysml.decision: SysML 8.2.2.6.1 states NonOccurrenceUsageMember : FeatureMembership = MemberPrefix ownedRelatedElement += NonOccurrenceUsageElement. The SysML Xtext is identical. The rule is the clause as written.

NullExpression.decision: Two spellings of the same thing: the keyword, or an empty pair of parentheses. The empty parentheses matter because they are also what an ArgumentList with no arguments looks like; which production applies is positional.

ObjectiveMember@sysml.decision: SysML 8.2.2.22 states ObjectiveMember : ObjectiveMembership = MemberPrefix 'objective' ownedRelatedElement += ObjectiveRequirementUsage. The SysML Xtext is identical. The rule is the clause as written.

ObjectiveRequirementUsage@sysml.decision: SysML 8.2.2.22 states ObjectiveRequirementUsage : RequirementUsage = UsageExtensionKeyword* ConstraintUsageDeclaration RequirementBody. The SysML Xtext is identical. The rule is the clause as written.

OccurrenceDefinition@sysml.decision: SysML 8.2.2.9.1 states OccurrenceDefinitionPrefix 'occurrence' 'def' Definition, and the SysML Xtext agrees (the same structure; the keyword pair is factored into a keyword rule, a renaming). The rule is the clause as written.

OccurrenceDefinitionPrefix@sysml.decision: SysML 8.2.2.9.1 states OccurrenceDefinitionPrefix : OccurrenceDefinition = BasicDefinitionPrefix? ( isIndividual ?= 'individual' ownedRelationship += EmptyMultiplicityMember )? DefinitionExtensionKeyword*. The SysML Xtext is identical. The rule is the clause as written.

OccurrenceUsage@sysml.decision: SysML 8.2.2.9.2 states OccurrenceUsage = OccurrenceUsagePrefix 'occurrence' Usage. The SysML Xtext factors the keyword into a keyword rule, a renaming. The rule is the clause as written.

OccurrenceUsageElement@sysml.decision: SysML 8.2.2.6.4 states OccurrenceUsageElement : Usage = StructureUsageElement | BehaviorUsageElement, and the SysML Xtext agrees (identical). The rule is the clause as written.

OccurrenceUsageMember@sysml.decision: SysML 8.2.2.6.1 states OccurrenceUsageMember : FeatureMembership = MemberPrefix ownedRelatedElement += OccurrenceUsageElement. The SysML Xtext is identical. The rule is the clause as written.

OccurrenceUsagePrefix@sysml.decision: SysML 8.2.2.9.2 states OccurrenceUsagePrefix : OccurrenceUsage = BasicUsagePrefix ( isIndividual ?= 'individual' )? ( portionKind = PortionKind { isPortion = true } )? UsageExtensionKeyword*. Deviation OccurrenceUsagePrefix (follow_xtext) adds EndUsagePrefix as an alternative to the BasicUsagePrefix group, as the SysML Xtext does and the general usage prefix already does. The `{ isPortion = true }` action is abstract syntax.

OwnedAnnotation.decision: As KerML 8.2.3.3.1 and SysML 8.2.2.4.1 both state it, so one shared unit: an annotation that owns exactly one AnnotatingElement, with no tokens of its own. The Xtext rule is identical.

OwnedConjugation@kerml.decision: As KerML 8.2.4.1.3 states it: the original type, either as a cross-reference `[QualifiedName]` or as a FeatureChain. The clause writes FeatureChain where the Xtext writes OwnedFeatureChain. KerML 8.2.4.3.5 defines `OwnedFeatureChain : Feature = FeatureChain`, so the two accept exactly the same tokens, and the rule follows the clause. This is a difference in which element owns the chain, not a disagreement about syntax. The same clause's Conjugation production writes FeatureChain in both of its positions, so the usage is consistent within the clause.

OwnedCrossFeature@kerml.decision: As KerML 8.2.4.3.1 states it: a BasicFeaturePrefix, then a FeatureDeclaration. This is the KerML variant (ADR-0014); SysML states OwnedCrossFeature as BasicUsagePrefix UsageDeclaration. The pilot KerML Xtext has no rule of this name, so there is no second opinion. Every part of BasicFeaturePrefix is optional, so a cross feature may be a FeatureDeclaration alone, which is how it appears in the corpus.

OwnedCrossFeature@sysml.decision: As SysML 8.2.2.6.2 states it: a BasicUsagePrefix, then a UsageDeclaration, producing a ReferenceUsage. This is the SysML variant (ADR-0014); KerML states OwnedCrossFeature as BasicFeaturePrefix FeatureDeclaration. The Xtext rule is identical.

OwnedCrossFeatureMember.decision: A membership that wraps exactly one OwnedCrossFeature, with no tokens of its own. KerML 8.2.4.3.1 and SysML 8.2.2.6.2 state the same body, `ownedRelatedElement += OwnedCrossFeature`, so this is one shared unit. The two languages do define OwnedCrossFeature differently: in KerML it is BasicFeaturePrefix FeatureDeclaration, and in SysML it is a ReferenceUsage, BasicUsagePrefix UsageDeclaration. That difference belongs to OwnedCrossFeature, not here, and the reference resolves to each language's own variant. The SysML Xtext rule agrees.

OwnedCrossMultiplicity.decision: KerML 8.2.5.5.1 and SysML 8.2.2.13.1 both state OwnedCrossMultiplicity : Feature = ownedRelationship += OwnedMultiplicity, and the SysML Xtext agrees. The rule is the clause as written.

OwnedCrossMultiplicityMember.decision: KerML 8.2.5.5.1 and SysML 8.2.2.13.1 both state OwnedCrossMultiplicityMember : OwningMembership = ownedRelatedElement += OwnedCrossMultiplicity, and the SysML Xtext agrees. The rule is the clause as written.

OwnedCrossSubsetting@kerml.decision: As KerML 8.2.4.3.3 states it: `OwnedCrossSubsetting : CrossSubsetting = GeneralType`. This is the KerML variant (ADR-0014). The Xtext writes a body of its own where the clause names GeneralType. The rule keeps the clause's reference and does not port that. GeneralType is its own unit, and the two variants of this production are split because the SysML clause states it differently.

OwnedCrossSubsetting@sysml.decision: As SysML 8.2.2.6.5 states it: `crossedFeature = [QualifiedName]`, or `crossedFeature = OwnedFeatureChain` with the chain owned by the relationship. The cross-reference parses a QualifiedName. The `{ ownedRelatedElement += ... }` action consumes no tokens. This is the SysML variant (ADR-0014). The Xtext states the same two alternatives.

OwnedDisjoining@kerml.decision: As KerML 8.2.4.1.4 states it: the disjoining type, either as a cross-reference `[QualifiedName]` or as a FeatureChain owned by the relationship. The clause writes FeatureChain where the Xtext writes OwnedFeatureChain. KerML 8.2.4.3.5 defines `OwnedFeatureChain : Feature = FeatureChain`, so the two accept exactly the same tokens, and the rule follows the clause. The same clause's Disjoining production writes FeatureChain in both of its positions.

OwnedExpression.decision: Eight alternatives, exactly as KerML 8.2.5.8.1 states them. The Xtext reduces the whole production to `ConditionalExpression`, which is not a narrower language but a precedence cascade: the pilot threads the operator tiers through a chain of rules so a generated LL parser can resolve them. That is a parser-generator technique, not a language fact, and porting it would make this grammar describe the pilot. The clause is the source and the clause lists eight.

OwnedExpressionReference.decision: `ownedRelationship += OwnedExpressionMember`. Typed as a FeatureReferenceExpression, so what is built refers to the expression rather than containing its evaluation.

OwnedFeatureChain@kerml.decision: A feature chain, as KerML 8.2.4.3.5 states it.

OwnedFeatureChain@sysml.decision: One feature chaining followed by one or more further ones, each after a `.`, as SysML 8.2.2.6.5 states it. A chain therefore has at least two segments by construction.

OwnedFeatureChainMember@kerml.decision: A feature chain, as KerML 8.2.5.8.2 states it.

OwnedFeatureChainMember@sysml.decision: An owned feature chain, as SysML 8.2.2.17.5 states it.

OwnedFeatureChaining.decision: `chainingFeature = [QualifiedName]`. Each segment of a chain is itself a qualified name, so `a::b.c::d` is two segments and not four.

OwnedFeatureInverting@kerml.decision: As KerML 8.2.4.3.6 states it: the inverting feature, either as a cross-reference `[QualifiedName]`, which parses a QualifiedName, or as an owned feature chain. The `{ ownedRelatedElement += ... }` action consumes no tokens. The Xtext states the same two alternatives. Both alternatives can begin with a name, so a parser decides between them after it. Neither QualifiedName nor OwnedFeatureChain is defined in this clause, so exactly where they diverge is for their own units to establish.

OwnedFeatureMember@kerml.decision: A member prefix and a feature element, exactly as KerML 8.2.4.1.6 states it. No keyword: this is the plain way a feature becomes a member of a type, and it is the form nearly every feature in a corpus file takes.

OwnedFeatureTyping@kerml.decision: As KerML 8.2.4.3.2 states it: `OwnedFeatureTyping : FeatureTyping = GeneralType`. This is the KerML variant (ADR-0014). The Xtext writes a body of its own where the clause names GeneralType. The rule keeps the clause's reference and does not port that. GeneralType is its own unit, and the two variants of this production are split because the SysML clause states it differently.

OwnedFeatureTyping@sysml.decision: As SysML 8.2.2.6.5 states it: `type = [QualifiedName]`, or `type = OwnedFeatureChain` with the chain owned by the relationship. The cross-reference parses a QualifiedName. The `{ ownedRelatedElement += ... }` action consumes no tokens. This is the SysML variant (ADR-0014). The Xtext states the same two alternatives.

OwnedMultiplicity@kerml.decision: As KerML 8.2.5.11 states it: a membership wrapping one OwnedMultiplicityRange, which the same clause defines as MultiplicityBounds, the bracketed `[lower..upper]` form. This is the KerML variant (ADR-0014); SysML wraps a MultiplicityRange, which it defines directly as the bracketed form. The Xtext rule is identical.

OwnedMultiplicity@sysml.decision: As SysML 8.2.2.6.6 states it: a membership wrapping one MultiplicityRange, which the same clause defines as `'[' ( MultiplicityExpressionMember '..' )? MultiplicityExpressionMember ']'`. This is the SysML variant (ADR-0014). KerML wraps an OwnedMultiplicityRange instead, which is why the production is split. The Xtext rule is identical.

OwnedMultiplicityRange@kerml.decision: As KerML 8.2.5.11 states it: a MultiplicityRange consisting only of MultiplicityBounds, the bracketed form with no `multiplicity` keyword, name or body. The Xtext rule is the same.

OwnedRedefinition@kerml.decision: As KerML 8.2.4.3.4 states it: `OwnedRedefinition : Redefinition = GeneralType`. This is the KerML variant (ADR-0014). The Xtext writes a body of its own where the clause names GeneralType. The rule keeps the clause's reference and does not port that. GeneralType is its own unit, and the two variants of this production are split because the SysML clause states it differently.

OwnedRedefinition@sysml.decision: As SysML 8.2.2.6.5 states it: `redefinedFeature = [QualifiedName]`, or `redefinedFeature = OwnedFeatureChain` with the chain owned by the relationship. The cross-reference parses a QualifiedName. The `{ ownedRelatedElement += ... }` action consumes no tokens. This is the SysML variant (ADR-0014). The Xtext states the same two alternatives.

OwnedReferenceSubsetting@kerml.decision: As KerML 8.2.4.3.3 states it: `OwnedReferenceSubsetting : ReferenceSubsetting = GeneralType`. This is the KerML variant (ADR-0014). The Xtext writes a body of its own where the clause names GeneralType. The rule keeps the clause's reference and does not port that. GeneralType is its own unit, and the two variants of this production are split because the SysML clause states it differently.

OwnedReferenceSubsetting@sysml.decision: As SysML 8.2.2.6.5 states it: `referencedFeature = [QualifiedName]`, or `referencedFeature = OwnedFeatureChain` with the chain owned by the relationship. The cross-reference parses a QualifiedName. The `{ ownedRelatedElement += ... }` action consumes no tokens. This is the SysML variant (ADR-0014). The Xtext states the same two alternatives. The clause writes the action as `{ ownedRelatedElement += referenceFeature }`, naming `referenceFeature` where the property is `referencedFeature`. The action consumes no tokens, so the rule is unaffected. Whether OMG has filed this was not searched.

OwnedRelatedElement@kerml.decision: As KerML 8.2.3.1 states it: a NonFeatureElement or a FeatureElement. The Xtext rule is identical.

OwnedSpecialization@kerml.decision: KerML 8.2.4.1.2 states OwnedSpecialization : Specialization = GeneralType. The KerML Xtext inlines GeneralType's two alternatives, `general = [QualifiedName] | ownedRelatedElement += OwnedFeatureChain`; the inlining is not ported. The rule is the clause as written.

OwnedSubclassification.decision: KerML 8.2.4.2.2 states OwnedSubclassification : Subclassification = superclassifier = [QualifiedName], and SysML 8.2.2.6.5 states the same cross-reference, spelling the property superClassifier. The property name is abstract syntax; the syntax is one cross-reference in both, so the unit is shared. The KerML Xtext agrees. A cross-reference [QualifiedName] is a ref to QualifiedName by the derivation's convention.

OwnedSubsetting@kerml.decision: As KerML 8.2.4.3.3 states it: `OwnedSubsetting : Subsetting = GeneralType`. This is the KerML variant (ADR-0014). The Xtext writes a body of its own where the clause names GeneralType. The rule keeps the clause's reference and does not port that. GeneralType is its own unit, and the two variants of this production are split because the SysML clause states it differently.

OwnedSubsetting@sysml.decision: As SysML 8.2.2.6.5 states it: `subsettedFeature = [QualifiedName]`, or `subsettedFeature = OwnedFeatureChain` with the chain owned by the relationship. The cross-reference parses a QualifiedName. The `{ ownedRelatedElement += ... }` action consumes no tokens. This is the SysML variant (ADR-0014). The Xtext states the same two alternatives.

OwnedTypeFeaturing@kerml.decision: As KerML 8.2.4.3.7 states it: `featuringType = [QualifiedName]`, a cross-reference only. Unlike the Owned* specialization targets, it has no feature-chain alternative. The Xtext rule is the same. The pack cites only the KerML clause, and the plan makes this one shared unit.

Package.decision: KerML 8.2.5.13 and SysML 8.2.2.5.1 state Package identically: ( ownedRelationship += PrefixMetadataMember )* PackageDeclaration PackageBody, and the KerML Xtext agrees. The productions it names are stated differently per language (SysML's PackageBody reads PackageBodyElement, KerML's reads NamespaceBodyElement), but Package's own body is the same text, so the unit is shared and each language resolves the references to its own variants.

PackageBody@kerml.decision: KerML 8.2.5.13 states PackageBody : Package = ';' | '{' ( NamespaceBodyElement | ownedRelationship += ElementFilterMember )* '}'. The KerML Xtext expands the body element into NamespaceMember | ElementFilterMember | AliasMember | Import, and its own comment says this is 'to avoid infinite loops in the incremental parser' — an LL workaround, not ported. The rule is the clause as written.

PackageBody@sysml.decision: SysML 8.2.2.5.1 states PackageBody : Package = ';' | '{' PackageBodyElement* '}'. The SysML Xtext expands PackageBodyElement into PackageMember | ElementFilterMember | AliasMember | Import, and its own comment says this is 'to avoid infinite loops in the incremental parser' — an LL workaround, not ported. The rule is the clause as written.

PackageBodyElement@sysml.decision: Four alternatives, as SysML 8.2.2.5.1 states them: a package member, an element filter member, an alias member, or an import. This is what a SysML root namespace, and a SysML package body, is a sequence of.

PackageDeclaration.decision: KerML 8.2.5.13 and SysML 8.2.2.5.1 both state PackageDeclaration : Package = 'package' Identification. The KerML Xtext writes 'package' Identification?; whether that '?' changes the language depends on Identification's own rule, which is not in this pack, so it is not read as a disagreement and the rule is the clause as written. Corpus lines such as `package AddressBookModel {` fit it.

PackageMember@sysml.decision: A member prefix, then a definition element or a usage element, as SysML 8.2.2.5.1 states it.

ParameterRedefinition.decision: `redefinedFeature = [QualifiedName]`. A named argument's left side redefines the parameter it supplies, so it is a reference to that parameter rather than a new name.

PartDefinition@sysml.decision: SysML 8.2.2.11 states OccurrenceDefinitionPrefix 'part' 'def' Definition, and the SysML Xtext agrees (the same structure; the keyword pair is factored into a keyword rule, a renaming). The rule is the clause as written.

PartUsage@sysml.decision: SysML 8.2.2.11 states PartUsage = OccurrenceUsagePrefix 'part' Usage. The SysML Xtext factors the keyword into a keyword rule, a renaming. The rule is the clause as written.

PayloadFeature@kerml.decision: KerML 8.2.5.9.2's PayloadFeature is malformed (three '(' and two ')', KERML11-115), so it is not derived as written. Deviation PayloadFeature (follow_spec) repairs it to the reading every well-formed source states: the first two alternatives as printed, `OwnedFeatureTyping OwnedMultiplicity?`, and `OwnedMultiplicity OwnedFeatureTyping` with the typing mandatory. The minimal paren repair would instead make a bare multiplicity a payload; the deviation records why that reading is rejected. The Xtext agrees with the repaired rule, apart from writing Identification? on the first two alternatives.

PayloadFeature@sysml.decision: SysML 8.2.2.16 states PayloadFeature : Feature = Identification? PayloadFeatureSpecializationPart ValuePart? | ownedRelationship += OwnedFeatureTyping ( ownedRelationship += OwnedMultiplicity )? | ownedRelationship += OwnedMultiplicity ownedRelationship += OwnedFeatureTyping. The SysML Xtext's Payload fragment adds `Identification? ValuePart`; deviation PayloadFeature-sysml-value-alternative (follow_spec) declines it, with the adjudicator's dissent recorded. The rule is the clause as written.

PayloadFeatureMember@kerml.decision: As KerML 8.2.5.9.2 states it: a membership wrapping one PayloadFeature, with no tokens of its own. The clause assigns with `=` where other memberships use `+=`; the assignment operator consumes no tokens. The clause text is malformed in PayloadFeature, which prints three `(` against two `)`, filed as KERML11-115. That defect is PayloadFeature's own, and this production's text is sound. The Xtext rule agrees.

PayloadFeatureSpecializationPart.decision: KerML 8.2.5.9.2 states PayloadFeatureSpecializationPart : Feature = FeatureSpecialization+ MultiplicityPart? FeatureSpecialization* | MultiplicityPart FeatureSpecialization+. SysML 8.2.2.16 states the same except that it writes `( -> FeatureSpecialization )+`, carrying the pilot's `->` syntactic predicate into the specification text; the predicate steers an LL parser and does not change the language, so it is not ported and the two clauses state one rule, shared. The KerML Xtext also carries the predicate. The pack notes the clause's malformation is in PayloadFeature, not here. The rule is the KerML clause as written.

PayloadParameter@sysml.decision: A transcription of SysML 8.2.2.17.4. The Xtext differs in two ways and neither is a disagreement. It names its first alternative Payload, a rule that appears in no specification clause, where the clause writes PayloadFeature, which is a production with its own unit; the clause's name is taken. And it writes `Identification?` where the clause writes `Identification`, which is redundant rather than wider, because Identification is `( '<' NAME '>' )? ( declaredName = NAME )?` (8.2.2.2) and so already derives empty — the MultiplicityRange@kerml case again, and no deviation. The second alternative is what carries a timed or change trigger: TriggerValuePart is mandatory there, which is what separates `accept sig after 10[SI::s]` from the plain payload of `accept S`.

PayloadParameterMember@sysml.decision: A transcription of SysML 8.2.2.17.4: `ownedRelatedElement += PayloadParameter`. It contributes no tokens; the payload's own syntax, including the trigger expression forms, is entirely in PayloadParameter. It is the mandatory part of AcceptParameterPart, which is why every accept has a payload even where the text names only a type.

PerformActionUsage@sysml.decision: SysML 8.2.2.17.2 states PerformActionUsage = OccurrenceUsagePrefix 'perform' PerformActionUsageDeclaration ActionBody. The SysML Xtext is identical. The rule is the clause as written.

PerformActionUsageDeclaration@sysml.decision: SysML 8.2.2.17.2 states PerformActionUsageDeclaration : PerformActionUsage = ( ownedRelationship += OwnedReferenceSubsetting FeatureSpecializationPart? | 'action' UsageDeclaration ) ValuePart?. The SysML Xtext writes UsageDeclaration? and factors 'action' into a keyword rule; UsageDeclaration is already nullable, so neither changes the language. The rule is the clause as written.

PortConjugation@sysml.decision: SysML 8.2.2.12 states PortConjugation = {}. The SysML Xtext writes {SysML::PortConjugation}, the same. The body is an action that creates a PortConjugation and consumes no tokens, so the rule is the empty sequence. The rule is the clause as written.

PortDefinition@sysml.decision: SysML 8.2.2.12 states PortDefinition = DefinitionPrefix 'port' 'def' Definition ownedRelationship += ConjugatedPortDefinitionMember, and the SysML Xtext agrees (the same structure; the keyword pair is factored into a keyword rule, a renaming). The rule is the clause as written. The clause's `{ conjugatedPortDefinition.ownedPortConjugator.originalPortDefinition = this }` and Note 1 are assignments on the abstract syntax, not syntax, and have no place in the rule.

PortUsage@sysml.decision: SysML 8.2.2.12 states PortUsage = OccurrenceUsagePrefix 'port' Usage. The SysML Xtext factors the keyword into a keyword rule, a renaming. The rule is the clause as written.

PortionKind@sysml.decision: SysML 8.2.2.9.2 states PortionKind = 'snapshot' | 'timeslice'. The SysML Xtext states the same two literals as an enum. The rule is the clause as written.

PortionUsage@sysml.decision: SysML 8.2.2.9.2 states PortionUsage : OccurrenceUsage = BasicUsagePrefix ( isIndividual ?= 'individual' )? portionKind = PortionKind UsageExtensionKeyword* Usage { isPortion = true }. The SysML Xtext is the same syntax, without the action. The `{ isPortion = true }` action is abstract syntax. The rule is the clause as written.

PositionalArgumentList.decision: One or more ArgumentMembers, comma separated.

Predicate@kerml.decision: KerML 8.2.5.7.3 states Predicate = TypePrefix 'predicate' ClassifierDeclaration FunctionBody. The KerML Xtext is identical. The rule is the clause as written.

PrefixMetadataAnnotation@kerml.decision: KerML 8.2.5.12 states PrefixMetadataAnnotation : Annotation = '#' ownedRelatedElement += PrefixMetadataFeature. The KerML Xtext is identical. The rule is the clause as written.

PrefixMetadataAnnotation@sysml.decision: SysML 8.2.2.27 states PrefixMetadataAnnotation : Annotation = '#' annotatingElement = PrefixMetadataUsage { ownedRelatedElement += annotatingElement }. The SysML Xtext writes '#' ownedRelatedElement += PrefixMetadataUsage, the same syntax with a different assignment. The `{ ownedRelatedElement += annotatingElement }` action is abstract syntax. The rule is the clause as written.

PrefixMetadataFeature@kerml.decision: As KerML 8.2.5.12 states it: one OwnedFeatureTyping, the metadata's type. The clause prints `PrefixMetadataFeature : MetadataFeature :` with a colon where every other production has `=`. KERML11-108 names this exact production as ending in a colon instead of an equals sign, so the defect is filed and the body after it reads unambiguously. The Xtext calls a MetadataTyping rule where the clause writes OwnedFeatureTyping. Where the Xtext narrows this to MetadataTyping, a QualifiedName naming a metaclass, the sources disagreed. The grammar-adjudicator decided follow_spec, because the metaclass requirement is a validation constraint, not syntax; see notes and the deviation PrefixMetadataTyping-chain.

PrefixMetadataMember@kerml.decision: As KerML 8.2.5.12 states it: `#` followed by one PrefixMetadataFeature, which the same clause defines as an OwnedFeatureTyping, so in practice `#` and a type name. This is the KerML variant (ADR-0014). SysML states the production with a PrefixMetadataUsage in place of the PrefixMetadataFeature, and that difference is why the production is split. The clause prints the PrefixMetadataFeature production with `:` where `=` belongs. That defect is in PrefixMetadataFeature's own text, not here, and its own unit should record it. The Xtext rule agrees.

PrefixMetadataMember@sysml.decision: As SysML 8.2.2.27 states it: `#` followed by one PrefixMetadataUsage, which the same clause defines as an OwnedFeatureTyping, so in practice `#` and a metadata definition name. This is the SysML variant (ADR-0014); KerML states the production with a PrefixMetadataFeature. The clause prints the property as `ownedRelatedEleemnt` and assigns it with `=`. Neither affects the syntax, since a property name and its assignment operator consume no tokens. The misspelling is filed with OMG as SYSML21-336, and the rule is unaffected. The Xtext writes `ownedRelatedElement +=` and otherwise agrees.

PrefixMetadataUsage@sysml.decision: As SysML 8.2.2.27 states it: one OwnedFeatureTyping, the metadata usage's definition. The Xtext calls a MetadataTyping rule where the clause writes OwnedFeatureTyping, and also carries a commented-out repetition of MetadataBodyUsageMember. Where the Xtext narrows this to MetadataTyping, a QualifiedName naming a metaclass, the sources disagreed. The grammar-adjudicator decided follow_spec, because the metaclass requirement is a validation constraint, not syntax; see notes and the deviation PrefixMetadataTyping-chain.

PrimaryExpression.decision: Two alternatives: a feature chain, or anything else primary.

QualifiedName.decision: An optional global-scope qualifier, then zero or more qualifying segments, then the name itself. The final NAME is not optional, so `A::` is not a qualified name and neither is `$::`.

RealValue.decision: Either a decimal point with an optional integer part and a required fractional or exponential part, or an exponential on its own. The integer part being optional is what makes `.5` a real; the fractional part being required is what keeps `5.` from being one.

Redefines.decision: As KerML 8.2.4.3.1 and SysML 8.2.2.6.5 both state it, so one shared unit: the REDEFINES terminal, then one OwnedRedefinition. KerML 8.2.2.7 and SysML 8.2.2.1.2 define REDEFINES identically, as `':>>' | 'redefines'`, and the rule writes it out as that choice. The Xtext fragment writes the same expansion.

Redefinition@kerml.decision: KerML 8.2.4.3.4 states Redefinition = ( 'specialization' Identification )? 'redefinition' SpecificType REDEFINES GeneralType RelationshipBody. The KerML Xtext writes the optional name part as `( 'specialization' Identification? )?`; the specification's Identification can already be empty, so the inner '?' adds nothing, and inlines SpecificType and GeneralType as `[QualifiedName] | OwnedFeatureChain`; the inlining is not ported. REDEFINES is the special lexical terminal of KerML 8.2.2.7, written out as keyword alternatives. The rule is the clause as written.

Redefinitions.decision: As KerML 8.2.4.3.1 and SysML 8.2.2.6.5 both state it, so one shared unit: one Redefines, then any number of further OwnedRedefinitions, separated by commas. The Xtext fragment is identical.

RefPrefix@sysml.decision: SysML 8.2.2.6.2 states RefPrefix : Usage = ( direction = FeatureDirection )? ( isDerived ?= 'derived' )? ( isAbstract ?= 'abstract' | isVariation ?= 'variation' )? ( isConstant ?= 'constant' )?, and the SysML Xtext agrees (identical). The rule is the clause as written.

ReferenceTyping.decision: `type = [QualifiedName]`. The brackets are the specification's notation for the result of resolving text parsed as a QualifiedName (KerML 8.2.3.4.1 note 3), so what parses here is a QualifiedName and the resolution is a later concern.

ReferenceUsage@sysml.decision: SysML 8.2.2.6.3 states ReferenceUsage = ( EndUsagePrefix | RefPrefix ) 'ref' Usage. The SysML Xtext factors the keyword into a keyword rule, a renaming. The rule is the clause as written.

References.decision: As KerML 8.2.4.3.1 and SysML 8.2.2.6.5 both state it, so one shared unit: the REFERENCES terminal, then exactly one OwnedReferenceSubsetting, with no comma-separated repetition. KerML 8.2.2.7 and SysML 8.2.2.1.2 define REFERENCES identically, as `'::>' | 'references'`, and the rule writes it out as that choice. The Xtext calls a ReferencesKeyword rule where the clauses name the terminal. The terminal is written out here.

RelationshipBody@kerml.decision: A semicolon, or braces around any number of relationship-owned elements, as KerML 8.2.3.1 states it.

RelationshipBody@sysml.decision: A semicolon, or braces around any number of owned annotations, as SysML 8.2.2.2 states it.

RelationshipOwnedElement@kerml.decision: As KerML 8.2.3.1 states it: an owned related element, which the same clause defines as NonFeatureElement | FeatureElement, or an owned annotation. The Xtext fragment is identical. RelationshipBody, in the same clause, repeats this inside braces.

RenderingDefinition@sysml.decision: SysML 8.2.2.26.4 states OccurrenceDefinitionPrefix 'rendering' 'def' Definition, and the SysML Xtext agrees (the same structure; the keyword pair is factored into a keyword rule, a renaming). The rule is the clause as written.

RenderingUsage@sysml.decision: SysML 8.2.2.26.4 states RenderingUsage = OccurrenceUsagePrefix 'rendering' Usage. The SysML Xtext factors the keyword into a keyword rule, a renaming. The rule is the clause as written.

RequirementBody@sysml.decision: SysML 8.2.2.21.1 states RequirementBody : Type = ';' | '{' RequirementBodyItem* '}'. The SysML Xtext uses a `=>` syntactic predicate, which exists to steer the pilot's LL parser and is not ported. The rule is the clause as written.

RequirementBodyItem@sysml.decision: SysML 8.2.2.21.1 states RequirementBodyItem : Type = DefinitionBodyItem | ownedRelationship += SubjectMember | ownedRelationship += RequirementConstraintMember | ownedRelationship += FramedConcernMember | ownedRelationship += RequirementVerificationMember | ownedRelationship += ActorMember | ownedRelationship += StakeholderMember. The SysML Xtext is identical. The rule is the clause as written.

RequirementConstraintMember@sysml.decision: SysML 8.2.2.21.1 states RequirementConstraintMember : RequirementConstraintMembership = MemberPrefix? RequirementKind ownedRelatedElement += RequirementConstraintUsage. The SysML Xtext writes MemberPrefix without the '?' and `kind = RequirementConstraintKind`, an enum of 'assume' | 'require', the same literals the clause's RequirementKind states. The clause writes MemberPrefix?; MemberPrefix is ( visibility = VisibilityIndicator )? and already nullable, so the '?' is kept as written and changes nothing. The rule is the clause as written.

RequirementConstraintUsage@sysml.decision: SysML 8.2.2.21.1 states RequirementConstraintUsage : ConstraintUsage = ownedRelationship += OwnedReferenceSubsetting FeatureSpecializationPart? RequirementBody | ( UsageExtensionKeyword* 'constraint' | UsageExtensionKeyword+ ) ConstraintUsageDeclaration CalculationBody. The SysML Xtext gives the first alternative CalculationBody; deviation RequirementConstraintUsage (follow_spec) keeps RequirementBody. The rule is the clause as written.

RequirementDefinition@sysml.decision: SysML 8.2.2.21.1 states OccurrenceDefinitionPrefix 'requirement' 'def' DefinitionDeclaration RequirementBody, and the SysML Xtext agrees (the same structure; the keyword pair is factored into a keyword rule, a renaming). The rule is the clause as written.

RequirementKind@sysml.decision: SysML 8.2.2.21.1 states RequirementKind : RequirementConstraintMembership = 'assume' { kind = 'assumption' } | 'require' { kind = 'requirement' }. The SysML Xtext has no RequirementKind rule; its RequirementConstraintKind enum has the same literals, 'assume' | 'require'. The { kind = ... } actions are abstract syntax. The rule is the clause as written.

RequirementUsage@sysml.decision: SysML 8.2.2.21.2 states RequirementUsage = OccurrenceUsagePrefix 'requirement' ConstraintUsageDeclaration RequirementBody. The SysML Xtext factors the keyword into a keyword rule, a renaming. The rule is the clause as written.

RequirementVerificationMember@sysml.decision: SysML 8.2.2.24 states RequirementVerificationMember : RequirementVerificationMembership = MemberPrefix 'verify' { kind = 'requirement' } ownedRelatedElement += RequirementVerificationUsage. The SysML Xtext writes the keyword as `kind = RequirementVerificationKind`, an enum whose one literal is 'verify'. The `{ kind = 'requirement' }` action is abstract syntax. The rule is the clause as written.

RequirementVerificationUsage@sysml.decision: SysML 8.2.2.24 states RequirementVerificationUsage : RequirementUsage = ownedRelationship += OwnedReferenceSubsetting FeatureSpecialization* RequirementBody | ( UsageExtensionKeyword* 'requirement' | UsageExtensionKeyword+ ) ConstraintUsageDeclaration RequirementBody. The SysML Xtext is the same, with 'requirement' as a keyword rule. The rule is the clause as written.

ResultExpressionMember@kerml.decision: A member prefix and an expression, with no terminating semicolon, as KerML 8.2.5.7.1 states it. The missing semicolon is what distinguishes a body's result expression from a member of it.

ResultExpressionMember@sysml.decision: An optional member prefix and an expression, with no terminating semicolon, exactly as SysML 8.2.2.19 writes it — including the `?` on MemberPrefix.

ReturnFeatureMember@kerml.decision: A member prefix, `return`, then the feature returned.

ReturnParameterMember@sysml.decision: SysML 8.2.2.19 states ReturnParameterMember : ReturnParameterMembership = MemberPrefix? 'return' ownedRelatedElement += UsageElement. The SysML Xtext writes MemberPrefix without the '?'. The clause writes MemberPrefix?; MemberPrefix is ( visibility = VisibilityIndicator )? and already nullable, so the '?' is kept as written and changes nothing. The rule is the clause as written.

RootNamespace@kerml.decision: Zero or more namespace body elements, exactly as KerML 8.2.3.4.1 states it. This is the start symbol of the KerML grammar: a .kerml file is a sequence of namespace members, aliases and imports with no enclosing declaration, and an empty file is a valid root namespace.

RootNamespace@sysml.decision: Zero or more package body elements, exactly as SysML 8.2.2.5.1 states it. This is the start symbol of the SysML grammar: a .sysml file is a sequence of package members, element filters, aliases and imports with no enclosing declaration, and an empty file is a valid root namespace.

SatisfactionFeatureValue@sysml.decision: A transcription of SysML 8.2.2.21.2. The clause and the Xtext state this production identically — `ownedRelatedElement += SatisfactionReferenceExpression` in both — so there is nothing to weigh. It contributes no tokens. Note that it carries no '=' or ':=' of its own, unlike the general FeatureValue of 8.2.2.6.2: the subject of a satisfaction is bound by position after 'by', not by an assignment operator, and this production exists to make that binding a FeatureValue in the model without any operator being written.

SatisfactionParameter@sysml.decision: A transcription of SysML 8.2.2.21.2. The clause and the Xtext state this production identically — `ownedRelationship += SatisfactionFeatureValue` in both — so there is nothing to weigh. It contributes no tokens: it is the reference usage that stands as the subject parameter of a satisfaction, and the subject's text is reached below it, through SatisfactionFeatureValue to a SatisfactionReferenceExpression and finally a FeatureChainMember. The 'by' that introduces the subject belongs to SatisfyRequirementUsage.

SatisfactionReferenceExpression@sysml.decision: A transcription of SysML 8.2.2.21.2. The clause and the Xtext state this production identically — `ownedRelationship += FeatureChainMember` in both — so there is nothing to weigh. It contributes no tokens: it is the feature reference expression that wraps the subject of a satisfaction, and everything written is the chain below it. Being a FeatureChainMember rather than a plain name is what lets the subject be `vehicle_design.engine_v1` as readily as `vehicle_design`.

SatisfactionSubjectMember@sysml.decision: A transcription of SysML 8.2.2.21.2. The clause and the Xtext state this production identically — `ownedRelatedElement += SatisfactionParameter` in both — so there is nothing to weigh. The production contributes no tokens of its own: it is the membership that carries the subject of a satisfaction, and everything visible is below it. The 'by' that introduces the subject belongs to SatisfyRequirementUsage, which is where the clause puts it (`( 'by' ownedRelationship += SatisfactionSubjectMember )?`), and the text of the subject itself is reached through SatisfactionParameter, a chain of four one-line productions ending at a FeatureChainMember.

SatisfyRequirementUsage@sysml.decision: SysML 8.2.2.21.2 states SatisfyRequirementUsage = OccurrenceUsagePrefix 'assert' ( isNegated ?= 'not' ) 'satisfy' ( OwnedReferenceSubsetting FeatureSpecializationPart? | 'requirement' UsageDeclaration ) ValuePart? ( 'by' SatisfactionSubjectMember )? RequirementBody. Deviation SatisfyRequirementUsage (follow_xtext) makes 'assert' and 'not' optional, as the SysML Xtext does and SysML 7.21.4 and the corpus require. The rest is the clause as written; the Xtext's UsageDeclaration? adds nothing, UsageDeclaration being nullable.

SelectExpression.decision: `.?` then a body. A distinct operator token, so unlike CollectExpression it needs no lookahead past the operator.

SendNode@sysml.decision: Adjudicated. One line of SysML 8.2.2.17.4 carries two defects, and the rule departs from the clause's literal text on both; each is recorded in deviations.json. First, the clause's second alternative ends in SendReceiverPart, which is defined nowhere in either specification, while SenderReceiverPart is defined two lines below in the same clause — a dangling reference repaired from the specification's own text (deviation SendReceiverPart-misspelling, follow_spec, SYSML21-408 open). Second, the clause writes ActionUsageDeclaration? where the Xtext and the clause's own three sibling declarations write ActionNodeUsageDeclaration?; those are different productions, the first carrying no 'action' keyword, and three files in the pinned corpus write exactly the keyword the literal reading would reject (deviation SendNode, follow_xtext, SYSML21-624 open). Not taken from the Xtext: its `( ActionBody | ( => ... ActionBody ) )` hoists the optional part into an explicit choice behind a '=>' syntactic predicate, an LL workaround for a parser generator this project does not use. The clause's `( ... )? ActionBody` says the same thing and is kept.

SendNodeDeclaration@sysml.decision: A transcription of SysML 8.2.2.17.4: `ActionNodeUsageDeclaration? 'send' ownedRelationship += NodeParameterMember SenderReceiverPart?`. The pinned pilot grammar states it identically at SysML.xtext:1511, as a fragment — an inlining mechanism of that parser generator, not a claim about the language. The payload parameter is mandatory and the sender/receiver part is not, which is what makes a bare `send x;` legal; where the receiver is written, SenderReceiverPart supplies both the 'via' and 'to' spellings.

SenderReceiverPart@sysml.decision: A transcription of SysML 8.2.2.17.4. The clause and the Xtext state this production identically, so there is nothing to weigh. The two alternatives are the two ways a send names its ends: 'via' a sender, optionally also 'to' a receiver; or no sender at all — an EmptyParameterMember, which contributes no tokens — and 'to' a receiver. The second alternative is why `send x to y` binds `y` as the receiver rather than the sender, and why the parameter positions come out the same in both spellings. This is the production SendNode's own clause line misspells as SendReceiverPart; see the deviation of that name.

SequenceExpressionList.decision: One expression with an optional trailing comma, or a comma-operator expression. The optional trailing comma on the single-element form is what distinguishes a one-element sequence from a parenthesised expression.

SequenceOperatorExpression.decision: The comma as an operator: one expression, a comma, then the rest of the list. Right-recursive through SequenceExpressionListMember, which is how a list of any length is built from a binary operator.

SourceEnd@sysml.decision: A transcription of SysML 8.2.2.9.3: `SourceEnd : ReferenceUsage = ( ownedRelationship += OwnedMultiplicity )?`. There is no second opinion to weigh — the pinned pilot grammar has no SourceEnd rule, as it has none for SourceEndMember or SourceSuccession above it — so the clause is the only source. The whole production is optional, so it derives the empty string, which is the usual case: a source succession names no source, because the source is the body item it follows. The multiplicity is the one thing that can be written for it.

SourceEndMember@sysml.decision: A transcription of SysML 8.2.2.9.3: `SourceEndMember : EndFeatureMembership = ownedRelatedElement += SourceEnd`. There is no second opinion to weigh — the pinned pilot grammar has no SourceEndMember rule, as it has none for SourceSuccession above it — so the clause is the only source. The production contributes no tokens of its own, and at most a multiplicity through SourceEnd, which is `( ownedRelationship += OwnedMultiplicity )?`. It is the end that a source succession leaves implicit: the source is the body item the succession follows, so the end exists in the model with nothing written for it.

SourceSuccession@sysml.decision: A transcription of SysML 8.2.2.9.3, which states the production in one line: `SourceSuccession : SuccessionAsUsage = ownedRelationship += SourceEndMember`.
