There is no second opinion to weigh — the pinned pilot grammar has no SourceSuccession rule at all, so the clause is the only source and the rule is taken from it directly. The production contributes at most a multiplicity of its own: its SourceEndMember holds a SourceEnd, which is `( ownedRelationship += OwnedMultiplicity )?`. The 'then' that makes a source succession visible belongs to SourceSuccessionMember, not here, and the target is the body item that follows, supplied by the enclosing body rather than by this rule.

SourceSuccessionMember@sysml.decision: SysML 8.2.2.9.3 states SourceSuccessionMember : FeatureMembership = 'then' ownedRelatedElement += SourceSuccession. The SysML Xtext has no SourceSuccessionMember rule; its body items use EmptySuccessionMember instead. The rule is the clause as written.

Specialization@kerml.decision: KerML 8.2.4.1.2 states Specialization = ( 'specialization' Identification )? 'subtype' SpecificType SPECIALIZES GeneralType RelationshipBody. The KerML Xtext writes the optional name part as `( 'specialization' Identification? )?`; the specification's Identification can already be empty, so the inner '?' adds nothing, and inlines SpecificType and GeneralType as `[QualifiedName] | OwnedFeatureChain`; the inlining is not ported. SPECIALIZES is the special lexical terminal of KerML 8.2.2.7, written out as keyword alternatives. The rule is the clause as written.

SpecializationPart@kerml.decision: KerML 8.2.4.1.1 states SpecializationPart : Type = SPECIALIZES ownedRelationship += OwnedSpecialization ( ',' ownedRelationship += OwnedSpecialization )*. SPECIALIZES is the special lexical terminal of KerML 8.2.2.7, written out as ':>' | 'specializes'. The KerML Xtext is identical. The rule is the clause as written.

SpecificType@kerml.decision: KerML 8.2.4.1.2 states SpecificType : Specialization : specific = [QualifiedName] | specific += OwnedFeatureChain { ownedRelatedElement += specific }. The definition line ends in ':' where '=' belongs; deviation SpecificType (follow_spec, citing KERML11-108) reads it as a definition, as the production is referenced from Specialization, Subsetting and Redefinition. The pilot Xtext has no SpecificType rule; it inlines the two alternatives. The body is unambiguous: a cross-reference, a ref to QualifiedName by convention, or an OwnedFeatureChain. The `{ ownedRelatedElement += specific }` action is abstract syntax.

StakeholderMember@sysml.decision: SysML 8.2.2.21.1 states StakeholderMember : StakeholderMembership = MemberPrefix ownedRelatedElement += StakeholderUsage. The SysML Xtext is identical. The rule is the clause as written.

StakeholderUsage@sysml.decision: SysML 8.2.2.21.1 states StakeholderUsage : PartUsage = 'stakeholder' UsageExtensionKeyword* Usage. The SysML Xtext is identical. The rule is the clause as written.

StateAcceptActionUsage@sysml.decision: A transcription of SysML 8.2.2.18.1: `StateAcceptActionUsage : AcceptActionUsage = AcceptNodeDeclaration ActionBody`. There is no second opinion to weigh — the pinned pilot grammar defines no rule of this name, factoring all four State*ActionUsage forms into PerformedActionUsage (SysML.xtext:1811) instead. The clause's decomposition is taken, as it was on StateActionUsage. The 'accept' keyword lives in AcceptNodeDeclaration, not here, which is what keeps this production the same shape as its three siblings.

StateActionUsage@sysml.decision: SysML 8.2.2.18.1 states five alternatives; the Xtext states two, `EmptyActionUsage ';' | PerformedActionUsage ActionBody`. This looks like a disagreement and is not one. PerformedActionUsage (SysML.xtext:1811) is `PerformActionUsageDeclaration | AcceptNodeDeclaration | SendNodeDeclaration | AssignmentNodeDeclaration`, and the clause's four named alternatives are exactly those four declarations each followed by ActionBody (StatePerformActionUsage = PerformActionUsageDeclaration ActionBody, and so on for accept, send and assignment). The Xtext has simply factored the shared ActionBody out of the four; the two accept the same language. The clause's form is taken because its four productions each have a unit and PerformedActionUsage appears in no clause, so factoring would leave four derived units unreachable and put the distinction in a name the specification does not define.

StateAssignmentActionUsage@sysml.decision: A transcription of SysML 8.2.2.18.1: `StateAssignmentActionUsage : AssignmentActionUsage = AssignmentNodeDeclaration ActionBody`. There is no second opinion to weigh — the pinned pilot grammar defines no rule of this name, factoring the four State*ActionUsage forms into PerformedActionUsage (SysML.xtext:1811). The clause's decomposition is taken, as it was on StateActionUsage. The 'assign' keyword and the ':=' both live in AssignmentNodeDeclaration, so this production adds only the body.

StateBodyItem@sysml.decision: SysML 8.2.2.18.1 states StateBodyItem : Type = NonBehaviorBodyItem | ( ownedRelationsup += SourceSuccessionMember )? ownedRelationship += BehaviorUsageMember ( ownedRelationship += TargetTransitionUsageMember )* | ownedRelationship += TransitionUsageMember | ownedRelationship += EntryActionMember ( ownedRelationship += EntryTransitionMember )* | ownedRelationship += DoActionMember | ownedRelationship += ExitActionMember. The SysML Xtext inlines NonBehaviorBodyItem's alternatives, names the optional leading member EmptySuccessionMember where the clause names SourceSuccessionMember, and uses `=>` syntactic predicates; the inlining, the renamed productions and the predicates are not ported, since the clause names its own productions. `ownedRelationsup` is a misspelt property in an assignment, not syntax. The rule is the clause as written.

StateDefBody@sysml.decision: SysML 8.2.2.18.1 states StateDefBody : StateDefinition = ';' | ( isParallel ?= 'parallel' )? '{' StateBodyItem* '}'. The SysML Xtext references its own StateBodyPart where the clause writes StateBodyItem*; StateBodyPart is not a specification production and is not ported. The rule is the clause as written.

StateDefinition@sysml.decision: SysML 8.2.2.18.1 states OccurrenceDefinitionPrefix 'state' 'def' DefinitionDeclaration StateDefBody, and the SysML Xtext agrees (the same structure; the keyword pair is factored into a keyword rule, a renaming). The rule is the clause as written.

StatePerformActionUsage@sysml.decision: A transcription of SysML 8.2.2.18.1: `StatePerformActionUsage : PerformActionUsage = PerformActionUsageDeclaration ActionBody`. There is no second opinion to weigh — the pinned pilot grammar defines no rule of this name, because it factors the four State*ActionUsage forms into PerformedActionUsage with ActionBody pulled out (SysML.xtext:1811), which reaches the same language by a different decomposition. The clause's decomposition is taken, as it was on StateActionUsage, so that each of the four named productions exists and the choice between them stays where the specification puts it. Note that this production carries no 'perform' keyword: the full PerformActionUsage has `OccurrenceUsagePrefix 'perform'` before the declaration (8.2.2.17.2), and a state subaction omits both, which is what makes `entry performSelfTest;` a perform action written as a bare reference.

StateSendActionUsage@sysml.decision: A transcription of SysML 8.2.2.18.1: `StateSendActionUsage : SendActionUsage` followed by `SendNodeDeclaration ActionBody`. The header is missing its '=' — see notes — but the body is unambiguous and its three siblings in the same clause have the identical shape, so the rule is read as `SendNodeDeclaration ActionBody`. There is no second opinion to weigh: the pinned pilot grammar defines no rule of this name, factoring the four forms into PerformedActionUsage (SysML.xtext:1811). The clause's decomposition is taken, as it was on StateActionUsage.

StateUsage@sysml.decision: SysML 8.2.2.18.2 states StateUsage = OccurrenceUsagePrefix 'state' ActionUsageDeclaration StateUsageBody. The SysML Xtext factors the keyword into a keyword rule, a renaming. The rule is the clause as written.

StateUsageBody@sysml.decision: SysML 8.2.2.18.2 states StateUsageBody : StateUsage = ';' | ( isParallel ?= 'parallel' )? '{' StateBodyItem* '}'. The SysML Xtext references its own StateBodyPart, a `=> StateBodyItem*` behind a syntactic predicate, which is not ported. The rule is the clause as written.

Step@kerml.decision: A feature prefix, `step`, an optional declaration, an optional value and a type body. The declaration is OPTIONAL — BY ANALOGY WITH ITS THREE SIBLINGS AND NOT ON A CITATION. KERML11-181 does not name this clause. See the notes; this is the weakest of the four rulings and the corpus cannot check it.

Structure@kerml.decision: KerML 8.2.5.3 states Structure = TypePrefix 'struct' ClassifierDeclaration TypeBody. The KerML Xtext is identical. The rule is the clause as written.

StructureUsageElement@sysml.decision: SysML 8.2.2.6.4 states StructureUsageElement : Usage = OccurrenceUsage | IndividualUsage | PortionUsage | EventOccurrenceUsage | ItemUsage | PartUsage | ViewUsage | RenderingUsage | PortUsage | ConnectionUsage | InterfaceUsage | AllocationUsage | Message | FlowUsage | SuccessionFlowUsage. The SysML Xtext is identical. The rule is the clause as written.

StructureUsageMember@sysml.decision: SysML 8.2.2.6.1 states StructureUsageMember : FeatureMembership = MemberPrefix ownedRelatedElement += StructureUsageElement. The SysML Xtext is identical. The rule is the clause as written.

Subclassification@kerml.decision: KerML 8.2.4.2.2 states Subclassification = ( 'specialization' Identification )? 'subclassifier' subclassifier = [QualifiedName] SPECIALIZES superclassifier = [QualifiedName] RelationshipBody. The KerML Xtext writes the optional name part as `( 'specialization' Identification? )?`; the specification's Identification can already be empty, so the inner '?' adds nothing, and otherwise agrees. SPECIALIZES is the special lexical terminal of KerML 8.2.2.7, written out as keyword alternatives. The rule is the clause as written.

SubclassificationPart@sysml.decision: SysML 8.2.2.6.5 states SubclassificationPart : Classifier = SPECIALIZES ownedRelationship += OwnedSubclassification ( ',' ownedRelationship += OwnedSubclassification )*. The SysML Xtext writes the same with SPECIALIZES as its SpecializesKeyword rule. SPECIALIZES is the special lexical terminal of SysML 8.2.2.1.2 (as KerML 8.2.2.7), written out as ':>' | 'specializes'. The rule is the clause as written.

SubjectMember@sysml.decision: SysML 8.2.2.21.1 states SubjectMember : SubjectMembership = MemberPrefix ownedRelatedElement += SubjectUsage. The SysML Xtext is identical. The rule is the clause as written.

SubjectUsage@sysml.decision: SysML 8.2.2.21.1 states SubjectUsage : ReferenceUsage = 'subject' UsageExtensionKeyword* Usage. The SysML Xtext is identical. The rule is the clause as written.

Subsets.decision: As KerML 8.2.4.3.1 and SysML 8.2.2.6.5 both state it, so one shared unit: the SUBSETS terminal, then one OwnedSubsetting. KerML 8.2.2.7 and SysML 8.2.2.1.2 define SUBSETS identically, as `':>' | 'subsets'`, and the rule writes it out as that choice. The Xtext fragment writes the same expansion.

Subsetting@kerml.decision: KerML 8.2.4.3.3 states Subsetting = ( 'specialization' Identification )? 'subset' SpecificType SUBSETS GeneralType RelationshipBody. The KerML Xtext writes the optional name part as `( 'specialization' Identification? )?`; the specification's Identification can already be empty, so the inner '?' adds nothing, and inlines SpecificType and GeneralType as `[QualifiedName] | OwnedFeatureChain`; the inlining is not ported. SUBSETS is the special lexical terminal of KerML 8.2.2.7, written out as keyword alternatives. The rule is the clause as written.

Subsettings.decision: As KerML 8.2.4.3.1 and SysML 8.2.2.6.5 both state it, so one shared unit: one Subsets, then any number of further OwnedSubsettings, separated by commas. The Xtext fragment is identical.

Succession@kerml.decision: A feature prefix, `succession`, the declaration, and the body, exactly as KerML 8.2.5.5.3 states it. The Xtext agrees. It is the same four-part shape as BindingConnector, with `first`/`then` in place of `of`/`=` inside the declaration.

SuccessionAsUsage@sysml.decision: SysML 8.2.2.13.3 states SuccessionAsUsage = UsagePrefix ( 'succession' UsageDeclaration )? 'first' s.ownedRelationship += ConnectorEndMember 'then' s.ownedRelationship += ConnectorEndMember UsageBody. The SysML Xtext writes UsageDeclaration? inside the group and DefinitionBody in place of UsageBody; neither is ported, since the clause names its own productions. The clause's `s.ownedRelationship` has a stray `s.` on both assignments; the prefix affects only the abstract-syntax assignment, not the syntax. The rule is the clause as written.

SuccessionDeclaration@kerml.decision: As KerML 8.2.5.5.3 states it, with two alternatives. The first is a FeatureDeclaration, optionally followed by `first` end `then` end. The second is an optional `all`, then optionally the two ends, with `first` itself optional. The Xtext fragment is identical. The second alternative derives the empty string. The clause writes the property as `s.isSufficient`, with a stray `s.` that no other production has. A property name consumes no tokens, so the rule is unaffected. Whether OMG has filed it was not searched. No corpus file uses the empty form or `all`; those rest on the clause and the Xtext.

SuccessionFlow@kerml.decision: Two keywords, `succession` then `flow`, around the same FlowDeclaration and TypeBody that Flow takes. The pair is what distinguishes this production, and the two words are separate keywords rather than one token.

SuccessionFlowUsage@sysml.decision: SysML 8.2.2.16 states SuccessionFlowUsage = OccurrenceUsagePrefix 'succession' 'flow' FlowDeclaration DefinitionBody. The SysML Xtext factors the keyword into a keyword rule, a renaming. The rule is the clause as written.

SuperclassingPart@kerml.decision: KerML 8.2.4.2.1 states SuperclassingPart : Classifier = SPECIALIZES ownedRelationship += OwnedSubclassification ( ',' ownedRelationship += OwnedSubclassification )*. SPECIALIZES is the special lexical terminal of KerML 8.2.2.7, written out as ':>' | 'specializes'. The KerML Xtext writes the same, with the member rule spelled Ownedsubclassification. The rule is the clause as written.

TargetSuccession@sysml.decision: A transcription of SysML 8.2.2.17.8. The Xtext accepts the same tokens and differs only in the name of the first member: it writes MultiplicitySourceEndMember, whose MultiplicitySourceEnd is `{SysML::ReferenceUsage} ( ownedRelationship += OwnedMultiplicity )?` (SysML.xtext:883-888), and the clause writes SourceEndMember, whose SourceEnd is `( ownedRelationship += OwnedMultiplicity )?` (8.2.2.9.3). Those are the same production under two names, so this is a naming difference rather than a disagreement, and the clause's name is taken because only SourceEndMember has a unit. The source end carries no reference of its own — at most a multiplicity — which is what makes this the target form: the source is the body item the succession follows, and only the target is written.

TargetTransitionUsage@sysml.decision: A transcription of SysML 8.2.2.18.3. The clause and the Xtext state this production identically once TransitionUsageKeyword is unwound to the single literal 'transition' it aliases (SysML.xtext:1850), so there is nothing to adjudicate. The three alternatives are kept as three: they are not collapsible into optional parts, because the first is distinguished by the 'transition' keyword, the second requires a trigger, and the third requires a guard, so collapsing them would admit a bare 'then' preceded by an effect alone. The whole group is optional, which is what makes `then Wait;` a target transition in its own right.

TargetTransitionUsageMember@sysml.decision: SysML 8.2.2.18.1 states TargetTransitionUsageMember : FeatureMembership = MemberPrefix ownedRelatedElement += TargetTransitionUsage. The SysML Xtext is identical. The rule is the clause as written.

TerminateNode@sysml.decision: A transcription of SysML 8.2.2.17.6: `OccurrenceUsagePrefix ActionNodeUsageDeclaration? 'terminate' ( ownedRelationship += NodeParameterMember )? ActionBody`. The Xtext writes the tail as `( ActionBody | -> ownedRelationship += NodeParameterMember ActionBody )`, which is the same language with the optionality hoisted into an explicit choice and a '->' syntactic predicate added to steer the parser generator past the ambiguity between an absent parameter and a present one. That predicate exists to satisfy a generator this project does not use, so it is not ported; the clause's `( ... )? ActionBody` is kept.

TextualRepresentation.decision: As KerML 8.2.3.3.3 and SysML 8.2.2.4.3 both state it, so one shared unit. An optional `rep` with an Identification, then `language` and a string naming the language, then the REGULAR_COMMENT body holding the text in that language. The Xtext writes `Identification?` inside the optional group, which is the same language because Identification is nullable.

TransitionAcceptActionUsage@sysml.decision: A transcription of SysML 8.2.2.18.3: `AcceptNodeDeclaration ( '{' ActionBodyItem* '}' )?`. There is no second opinion to weigh — the pinned pilot grammar defines no rule of this name. The tail is braces or nothing rather than an ActionBody, for the same reason as its three siblings: a transition effect is followed by the 'then' of the succession and so cannot take a ';' of its own. Note that this is an accept as an EFFECT, reached through 'do', and not the accept that is a transition's trigger, which is TriggerActionMember over TriggerAction.

TransitionAssignmentActionUsage@sysml.decision: A transcription of SysML 8.2.2.18.3: `AssignmentNodeDeclaration ( '{' ActionBodyItem* '}' )?`. There is no second opinion to weigh — the pinned pilot grammar defines no rule of this name. The tail is braces or nothing rather than an ActionBody, for the same reason as its three siblings: the transition's 'then' follows the effect directly.

TransitionPerformActionUsage@sysml.decision: A transcription of SysML 8.2.2.18.3: `PerformActionUsageDeclaration ( '{' ActionBodyItem* '}' )?`. There is no second opinion to weigh — the pinned pilot grammar defines no rule of this name, as it defines none for the other three transition effect forms — so the clause is the only source. The tail is braces or nothing, not an ActionBody: a transition effect cannot be terminated by a ';', because the 'then' of the transition's succession follows it. That is the one difference from StatePerformActionUsage, which is otherwise the same declaration.

TransitionSendActionUsage@sysml.decision: A transcription of SysML 8.2.2.18.3: `SendNodeDeclaration ( '{' ActionBodyItem* '}' )?`. There is no second opinion to weigh — the pinned pilot grammar defines no rule of this name. The tail is braces or nothing rather than an ActionBody, which is what the corpus shows: a send effect runs straight into the transition's 'then' with no terminator between them.

TransitionSuccession@sysml.decision: A transcription of SysML 8.2.2.18.3. The only difference from the Xtext is the name of the first member: the clause writes EmptyEndMember (`ownedRelatedElement += EmptyFeature`, and EmptyFeature is `{}`), the Xtext writes EmptySourceEndMember. Both derive empty, so the two accept the same language and this is a naming difference rather than a disagreement. The clause's name is taken, because EmptyEndMember is a production of the specification with its own unit and EmptySourceEndMember appears in no clause. A transition succession therefore contributes exactly the tokens of its ConnectorEndMember: the source end is implicit, supplied by the transition that owns it.

TransitionSuccessionMember@sysml.decision: A transcription of SysML 8.2.2.18.3. The clause and the Xtext state this production identically — `ownedRelatedElement += TransitionSuccession` in both — so there is nothing to weigh. It contributes no tokens of its own: it is the owning membership that holds the succession a transition ends with, and the 'then' that introduces it belongs to the transition productions that reference it, which is why the same member serves TransitionUsage, TargetTransitionUsage, GuardedSuccession and GuardedTargetSuccession without repeating the keyword.

TransitionUsage@sysml.decision: Straight from SysML 8.2.2.18.3. The Xtext differs in three places and none of them is a disagreement about the language. TransitionUsageKeyword is an alias for the single literal 'transition' (SysML.xtext:1850), so the rule writes the literal as the clause does. TransitionSourceMember is an Xtext-local name for a rule the specification already has: SysML.xtext:1884 gives it `memberElement = [Feature|QualifiedName] | ownedRelatedElement += OwnedFeatureChain`, which is FeatureChainMember's own clause text (`memberElement = [QualifiedName] | OwnedFeatureChainMember`, 8.2.2.17.5). The clause's reference is taken, since FeatureChainMember has a unit and TransitionSourceMember appears in no specification clause. The Xtext's `( UsageDeclaration? 'first' )?` against the clause's `( UsageDeclaration 'first' )?` is redundant rather than wider: UsageDeclaration is `Identification FeatureSpecializationPart?` (8.2.2.6.2) and Identification is `( '<' NAME '>' )? ( declaredName = NAME )?` (8.2.2.2), so it already derives empty and the two accept the same language. Same shape as the MultiplicityRange@kerml non-conflict, and not recorded as a deviation for the same reason.

TransitionUsageMember@sysml.decision: SysML 8.2.2.18.1 states TransitionUsageMember : FeatureMembership = MemberPrefix ownedRelatedElement += TransitionUsage. The SysML Xtext is identical. The rule is the clause as written.

TriggerAction@sysml.decision: A transcription of SysML 8.2.2.18.3: `TriggerAction : AcceptActionUsage = AcceptParameterPart`. The production is the body of a transition's trigger and carries no keyword: the 'accept' belongs to TriggerActionMember above it, which is why the same AcceptParameterPart serves here and inside a full accept action. That is what makes `accept ignitionCmd:IgnitionCmd via ignitionCmdPort` read as one trigger rather than as a nested accept action.

TriggerActionMember@sysml.decision: SysML 8.2.2.18.3 states `'accept' { kind = 'trigger' } ownedRelatedElement += TriggerAction`. The braced part is an assignment into the abstract syntax, not a token, so the concrete rule is the keyword followed by the trigger action. The Xtext writes `kind = TriggerFeatureKind ownedRelatedElement += TriggerAction`, where TriggerFeatureKind (SysML.xtext:1893) is an enum with exactly one literal, `trigger = 'accept'`. The two therefore accept the same single keyword and differ only in whether the kind is assigned by the enum or stated beside the literal — the same device the pilot uses for Expose's visibility. The clause's form is taken.

TriggerExpression@sysml.decision: SysML 8.2.2.17.4 states this production, but prints `kind = ( 'at | 'after' )` with no closing quote after at, so read literally the first literal never terminates and no rule can be derived. The quote is closed: the intended literals are 'at' and 'after', which the clause's own correctly-spelled 'when' beside them and the pilot grammar both confirm. Recorded as the deviation TriggerExpression, follow_spec; the defect is filed as SYSML21-401, open. Otherwise the clause is transcribed. The `kind =` assignments contribute no tokens, and the Xtext reaches the same three literals through two enums, TimeTriggerKind `'at' | 'after'` (SysML.xtext:1479) and ChangeTriggerKind `'when'` (1483) — the same device it uses for Expose's visibility and the transition feature kinds. The two branches differ in more than their keyword: a time trigger takes an ArgumentMember and a change trigger an ArgumentExpressionMember, which is the laziness distinction — the change trigger wraps its value in a reference so the expression is re-evaluated rather than evaluated once.

TriggerFeatureValue@sysml.decision: A transcription of SysML 8.2.2.17.4. The clause and the Xtext state this production identically — `ownedRelatedElement += TriggerExpression` in both — so there is nothing to weigh. It contributes no tokens, and like SatisfactionFeatureValue and FeatureBinding it carries no '=' or ':=': a trigger is bound to its parameter by position, so the FeatureValue exists in the model with no operator written.

TriggerValuePart@sysml.decision: A transcription of SysML 8.2.2.17.4. The clause and the Xtext state this production identically — `ownedRelationship += TriggerFeatureValue` in both — so there is nothing to weigh. It contributes no tokens; the trigger's keyword and argument are below it. The Xtext declares it a fragment, an inlining mechanism of that parser generator rather than a claim about the language.

Type@kerml.decision: KerML 8.2.4.1.1 states Type = TypePrefix 'type' TypeDeclaration TypeBody. The KerML Xtext is identical. The rule is the clause as written.

TypeBody@kerml.decision: A semicolon, or braces around any number of type body elements, as KerML 8.2.4.1.1 states it.

TypeBodyElement@kerml.decision: Four alternatives, exactly as KerML 8.2.4.1.1 states them: a non-feature member, a feature member, an alias member, or an import. This is the single production that says what may appear inside any type body, and TypeBody reaches it as `';' | '{' TypeBodyElement* '}'`.

TypeDeclaration@kerml.decision: KerML 8.2.4.1.1 states TypeDeclaration : Type = ( isSufficient ?= 'all' )? Identification ( ownedRelationship += OwnedMultiplicity )? ( SpecializationPart | ConjugationPart )+ TypeRelationshipPart*. The KerML Xtext writes the group once. That disagreement is adjudicated and recorded as deviation TypeDeclaration (follow_spec): the '+' is kept, and the rules against two conjugations or a conjugation with a specialization are left to validation, as PrefixMetadataTyping-chain did for its constraint. The rule is the clause as written.

TypeFeatureMember@kerml.decision: A member prefix, the `member` keyword, and a feature element, exactly as KerML 8.2.4.1.6 states it. The keyword is the entire concrete-syntax difference from OwnedFeatureMember, which is otherwise the identical shape.

TypeFeaturing@kerml.decision: KerML 8.2.4.3.7 states TypeFeaturing = 'featuring' ( Identification 'of' )? featureOfType = [QualifiedName] 'by' featuringType = [QualifiedName] RelationshipBody. The KerML Xtext writes `( Identification? 'of' )?`; the specification's Identification can already be empty, so the inner '?' adds nothing. The rule is the clause as written.

TypeFeaturingPart@kerml.decision: As KerML 8.2.4.3.1 states it: `featured by` and one or more OwnedTypeFeatures, separated by commas. The clause misspells the first property as `ownedRelatioship`, and the repetition assigns to `ownedTypeFeaturing` where the Xtext and the first element use ownedRelationship. Neither affects the syntax, since a property name consumes no tokens, so the rule is unaffected. The Xtext writes `ownedRelationship +=` in both places and otherwise agrees.

TypePrefix@kerml.decision: KerML 8.2.4.1.1 states TypePrefix : Type = ( isAbstract ?= 'abstract' )? ( ownedRelationship += PrefixMetadataMember )*. The KerML Xtext is identical. The rule is the clause as written.

TypeReferenceMember.decision: `ownedMemberFeature = TypeReference`. Identical in what it parses to TypeResultMember; they differ only in the membership metaclass each builds, which is abstract syntax and not syntax.

TypeRelationshipPart@kerml.decision: Four alternatives, as KerML 8.2.4.1.1 states them. The Xtext fragment lists the same four in the same order. The same clause shows DisjoiningPart beginning with `disjoint from`. The other three are not fully shown in this pack, so whether they overlap is for their own units to establish.

TypeResultMember.decision: `ownedMemberFeature = TypeReference`, as a ResultParameterMembership rather than a ParameterMembership. Same text, different membership.

TypedBy@kerml.decision: As KerML 8.2.4.3.1 states it: the TYPED_BY terminal, then one OwnedFeatureTyping. TYPED_BY is one of the special lexical terminals of KerML 8.2.2.7, `':' | 'typed' 'by'`, and the rule writes it out as that choice. This is the KerML variant (ADR-0014). SysML uses its DEFINED_BY terminal, `':' | 'defined' 'by'`, and a FeatureTyping. The Xtext fragment writes the same expansion.

TypedBy@sysml.decision: As SysML 8.2.2.6.5 states it: the DEFINED_BY terminal, then one FeatureTyping. DEFINED_BY is one of SysML's special lexical terminals, stated in 8.2.2.1.2 as `':' | 'defined' 'by'`, and the rule writes it out as that choice. This is the SysML variant (ADR-0014); KerML writes TYPED_BY, whose keyword form is `typed by`. The Xtext calls a DefinedByKeyword rule where the clause names the terminal. The specification's terminal is written out here and the Xtext rule is not referenced, so the rule's tokens come from the clause alone.

SysML's Typings repeats FeatureTyping instead, which also admits a ConjugatedPortTyping, and that is why the production is split. The Xtext fragment is identical.

VisibilityIndicator.decision: Three keywords, in the order KerML 8.2.3.4.1 states them. This is the only production in the membership prefix that contributes a terminal, and every visibility a member can carry is one of these three.

WhileLoopNode@sysml.decision: A transcription of SysML 8.2.2.17.7. The clause and the Xtext state this production identically, token for token (SysML.xtext:1615), so there is nothing to weigh. The two head alternatives are the same loop with and without a condition: 'while' takes an expression, 'loop' takes an EmptyParameterMember and so contributes no tokens of its own, which is how an unconditional loop still carries a condition parameter in the model. The 'until' tail carries its own ';' inside the optional group, so a loop without an until clause is terminated by its body's closing brace and not by a semicolon.
